#4215. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 30, 2026

Welcome to Devil's Night, the night before Halloween, where video games are best served scary. After tomorrow night – Halloween proper – no more scary video games allowed. At least not until mid-September, 2027. I'm sorry, I don't make the rules. Below you will find our weekend gaming recommendations (which is actually surprisingly light on scary games – apologies), but before that, here are some of the biggest stories of the week.

Phantom Blade Zero is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and it’s certainly one of the most impressive to watch. Beijing-based developer S-Game uses China’s Wuxia brand of action (which was actually banned for some time during the 20th Century by the country’s government) to create a stylish, fluid, and hyper-engaging combat system. It will constantly leave you in awe that action combat can look this good. But looks aren’t everything. Fortunately, Phantom Blade Zero delivers on all fronts, with weapon mechanics so detailed that picking up a new blade can feel like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. The story won’t blow your socks off, but it’s certainly engaging and enticing enough to bring you through Phantom Blade Zero’s 40 or so hours of content. If you’re not interested in the “perfect ending,” which is the only satisfactory one in my opinion, you can complete the game in less than 30 hours. S-Game mixes high-octane combat with sprawling and rewarding exploration to create a must-play during this already busy season of games. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Phantom Blade Zero review, and if you are hopping in this weekend, be sure to check out my list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks I wish I knew before starting it.

If you have any fond memories of IllFonic’s ill-fated Friday the 13th: The Game as I do, you simply must play the studio’s latest, Halloween: The Game. It is essentially Friday the 13th with Michael Myers instead of Jason, but with a decade of lessons learned from the team’s teeth carving in other horror properties and games. You’re either Michael or a citizen; the former wants to kill you and all the NPCs in various suburban maps, while the latter must rescue as many NPCs as possible while staying alive themselves. It’s that classic cat-and-mouse formula IllFonic is the master of, but with all the style, substance, and synths of John Carpenter’s Halloween masterpiece. Plus, Halloween: The Game features IllFonic’s first crack at a single-player campaign, and while it’s largely a tutorial for playing as Michael, if you’re a Halloween mega-fan like me, it’s worth checking out if only to take part in some of the film’s most iconic kills. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Halloween: The Game review here, and if you’re hopping in this weekend, there’s a new map, additional Halloween-themed cosmetics to unlock, and more waiting for you.

Overwatch is in the midst of its Halloween event, which have always historically been pretty interesting. This year it's Mystery Madness: Graveyard Games. In it, you begin by picking one of three characters in a random role. And then, as the game progresses, you choose perks that upgrade, alter, or completely change what your character can do. It can get really chaotic where by round three characters like Orisa might be three times her normal size or Torbjorn might have placed a giant turret on Mercy's making her a flying death machine. There are also Halloween skins, as well.

Tom the Postgirl is an odd little adventure that I'd recommend to fans of Untitled Goose Game. You play as Tom, a creepy girl who's tasked with delivering packages to the people of her wacky town, which is depicted with storybook-style illustrations and a color palette limited to black, white, and red. On the surface, you're delivering packages, but the game's real story is based on Tom's tendency to peep where she shouldn't, peering into townsfolks' windows to watch their odd lives. On house is full of kids who live like dogs; another has a couple with a bizarre obsession with tickling. You never know what each window might reveal, and I quickly sympathized with (and enabled) Tom's compulsion. You also have the capacity to cause quite a bit of trouble by stomping on flowers, haphazardly snipping strings and cords, or even stealing packages and using them for your own mischievous purposes. It's a pretty short experience, completable in just a few hours, making it a nice palate cleanser between the massive releases at the end of the year.

This Devolver Digital-published game has a simple but head-turning premise. You’re a profoundly angry woman who returns to her small hometown armed with nothing but a sledgehammer, which she uses to smash everything in sight. The town is also inhabited by robots possessing human consciousnesses. Swinging the hammer can either punch holes through walls or, with enough force, reduce entire buildings to rubble. But why is she doing this? Why is she so mad? A big part of Virtue and a Sledgehammer’s allure is its fascinating and well-written tale about the protagonist’s strained relationships with her sister and mother. Learning more about their lives requires you to keep smashing, but the more you learn, the more you begin to question whether smashing everything is actually a good idea.

This bizarre indie blends fun match-3 puzzle-solving with tower defense gameplay wrapped around a funny but surreal story. The match-3 gameplay involves sliding tiles to match geographic elements like castles, trees, and rivers to collect resources that feed into the tower defense portion. Depending on how the board looks when the puzzle portion ends, you send troops (sustained by the resources you collected) to attack/defend against rival castles and gather more items; board positioning determines how well this can go. The two mechanics feed into each other to create a fun loop that grows in complexity as new mechanics are introduced. Did I mention the game is also very weird? The silly tale centers on a medieval court designating you the chosen savior to rescue their lost queen (and many other tasks), and the dumb tone adds personality to a sometimes dry genre. Titanium Court charmed and impressed us when it launched on PC earlier this year, and now console and mobile players get their chance to hold court.

Sword of the Sea is a beautiful, 2025 game about surfing through the sand atop a floating sword. It recalls Journey, the emotional 2012 PlayStation game, which makes sense as it comes from the artists and developers that worked on that game, developer Giant Squid. Giant Squid also made 2016's Abzû and 2020's The Pathless. It's a talented team and Sword of the Sea maintains that reputation. And now you can play it on Switch 2. You can read my full review of the game (though this review pertains to the PlayStation 5 version) right here.

Cities: Skylines arrived on PC more than a decade ago, but is still revered as one of the greatest modern city-builders. Even now, three years after the sequel's release, Paradox continues supporting and porting the original game. A couple years after its initial release, Cities: Skylines received a strong console port, which did an admirable job of adapting the controls to gamepads, but the Switch version was always the weakest of the bunch. As of this week, Switch 2 owners can play a less compromised version, expanding the Switch's 9-tile limit to a much larger 25-tile limit, as well as better performance and textures, better control panels, and a ton of DLC and added content. And on top of that, if you own the Switch 1 version, you get a deep discount on the Switch 2 version.

While not specifically about this new Switch 2 version, you can read our original reviews of the base PC version here, and the base console version here.

Minecraft has held its dominant spot in pop culture for so long that it's easy to forget a simple fact about it: the game is awesome. This week, it's coming to Switch 2, giving potential miners another platform to explore procedurally-generated caves in. You've certainly heard of it, and you've probably played it, but I still feel it often doesn't get the flowers it deserves in high-level critical discussions about games, despite its regular cadence of major updates. The opening gameplay loop is so satisfying that for many of my peers, whether they regularly play video games or not, it's only a matter of time before they boot up a new world again. While you can never play the game for the first time again, if you haven't checked it out in a couple years, you might be surprised by the amount of new blocks, materials, and mobs they've added in recent updates. And if you've never played before, the Switch 2 launch is as good a time as any to see what all the fuss is about.

The card game incarnation of Arkham Horror remains one of the best narrative-driven and horror-themed tabletop games around, and it's an easy recommendation if you're looking for something engaging to dive into on Halloween night. Rooted in the monsters and mysteries of the Cthulhu Mythos, this living card game is built on major core sets and expansions. But unlike a TCG, each new installment has the same cards included, fueling the cooperative adventures you'll undertake together with your fellow players. Last year Arkham Horror: The Card Game did something of a soft relaunch for a chapter 2 of its narrative, and that new core set is an ideal place to jump on  play. Players each control an individual investigator as they explore arcane and weird mysteries, confront monsters, and unfold plots of cultists, ancient entities, and forbidden lore. For fans of cosmic horror storytelling, it's an easy pick.

#4213. 8 Best Anime Where Friendship is Built Through Small, Everyday Moments

Usama Mehmood is a Senior Writer at DualShockers with more than five years of experience in the video game industry. He has been writing professionally since 2021 and covering games since 2022, with work spanning guides, lists, reviews, and features across action-adventure games, JRPGs, open-world titles, racing games,

Oh, the sweet art of life known as friendship; it’s beautiful. It makes us realize just how deep human connections are forged, and that this extends to fictional media, whether it be your favorite bromances in gaming or just some of the best presentations of this bond showcased in movies, shows, or even anime.And you see, that’s exactly where some of my expertise lies, both professionally and personally. Being the only child of my parents, the only kind of sibling-like relationship I’ve had growing up, and even now, are my countless friends I’ve met online or IRL. Call it a “My friends are my Power” situation.

This list goes into extensive detail on the best romance anime where falling in love is just the beginning, but these shows prove that happily ever after is never that simple.

So, thinking about them and then my rather intermediate experience with anime, I woke up today and figured, let’s discuss some of my hand-picked anime where friendship is built through small, everyday moments. Where, no matter the ongoing circumstances that may ensue, the main cast manages to grow an everlasting bond with each other until the end of the show’s runtime.

I bet only some hardcore Kyoto Animation fans have seen this show, but trust me, it’s such a warm ray of sunshine. The series follows Tamako, a cheerful schoolgirl who spends most of her time helping at her family's mochi shop. Between school and her responsibilities at the shop, she shares plenty of moments with her best friends, Midori and Kanna.

But that balance is exactly what creates this sweet blend of friendship with the everyday life of a neighbourhood shop, pretty much exactly what you want from a slice-of-life anime. Oh, and if you want a romantic subplot payoff for Tamako, be sure to check out the sequel movie, Tamako Love Story, which is just as heartwarming as the OG show.

I’m switching tracks to a recent anime, one whose manga I read a bit of before the anime came into production. Skip and Loafer is mainly centered on Mitsumi Iwakura, a country girl who moves to Tokyo to attend a prestigious high school. While she's academically gifted, navigating the social dynamics of a city school proves more challenging than her studies. Fortunately, she meets Shima and gradually gets to know the other wildcard cast of classmates.

And while there is a romantic slow-burn development between Mitsumi and Shima, it’s not the main focus, since the main draw is Mitsumi slowly forming friendships with everyone through awkward conversations, shared school experiences, or small acts of consideration. It is genuinely a great slice-of-life seasonal show to watch from recent years of anime.

If you loved Frieren: Beyond Journey's End, this list goes into detail on the best anime to watch if you loved its delicate yet naturally paced vibe.

This one’s familiar to many readers, I hope. While Barakamon initially seems like it’s centered on a struggling calligrapher trying to reignite his creative spark, the story’s real soul comes from the surprising connections he builds after relocating to the Goto Islands.

Seishuu Handa starts out as a gifted but pretty snobbish artist who gets banished to a sleepy countryside village after an embarrassing incident, and he's so used to his quiet city life that he’s totally not ready for the lively locals who pop by his house for all sorts of reasons.

But you see, that’s the beauty of this show. Handa’s companionship with these locals slowly changes his outlook on life, especially through his interactions with the mischievous little girl named Naru. He develops a family-like bond here, and that's one reason this show is a perfect pick here.

This one’s actually one of my best friends’ favorite shows that he’s been begging me to watch for years, and I can honestly understand why. It's not only because of my fondness for Yuru Camp, but also because Non Non Biyori is one of THE defining Iyashikei (healing) shows on the block. It takes place in the sleepy countryside village of Asahigaoka, where a tiny school has only five students across different grade levels.

The anime lets you find plenty of warmth in these girls’ everyday interactions, whether it's Renge's amusing childlike observations or Natsumi and Komari's sibling antics. There is no kind of elaborate storyline either; it’s simply one of the coziest shows in the medium.

If you wanted peak relatability, then look no further than Hitoribocchi no Marumaru Seikatsu. That name is a mouthful for anyone preferring English titles, I know, but bear with me if it's your first time hearing about this cute little show because it’s fit for anyone who’s ever tried to get out of their comfort zone.

It’s about a girl named Hitori Bocchi (no, not the pink-haired anxiety rockstar) who is so anxious that talking to classmates feels like a final exam, but her goal of making friends is so adorable yet a little painful to watch. What I love is the show’s patience because her victories are tiny, like a successful greeting or a shared lunch, and the show treats each moment as a milestone.

With how many are airing, there are some Anime Series You’re Probably Missing Out on in 2026.

As much as I wanted it at the top for personal reasons, it’s also fine to include Yuru Camp here, because I could gush about it endlessly.

The series follows Rin Shima, a girl who enjoys camping alone, and Nadeshiko Kagamihara, an outgoing newcomer who shares her enthusiasm for exploring the outdoors, even if her initial impression here is sleeping on a bus stop bench at night. Their initial encounter eventually brings them into contact with a wider circle of friends at their school who also enjoy spending their free time camping as well.

The show is one of the best modern healing anime out there, especially since it teaches you so much about camping itself with Rin and the others’ trips. Even better is how it takes place at actual campsites and in key locations across Japan’s rural prefectures and towns.

It would’ve felt wrong not to mention K-On! on this list, especially given the whole emphasis on anime friendships with this list. What starts as an attempt to save her school's Light Music Club eventually becomes one of anime's most endearing friendships, as Yui Hirasawa joins Ritsu, Mio, and Tsumugi despite having practically no musical experience.

Of course, the girls spend plenty of time practising, but that's hardly what makes their relationship so enjoyable, since their afternoons are just as likely to involve drinking tea, chatting about random, inconsequential things, or finding excuses to avoid doing any actual work. Even after Azusa joins the club, watching this group become increasingly comfortable with one another is a genuine delight.

To me, if there’s one anime that defines a goofy, whimsical yet endearing friendship, it's Azumanga Daioh. Originally released in 2002, this beloved slice-of-life comedy follows six high school girls with wildly different personalities: the exceptionally gifted Chiyo Mihama, the absent-minded Osaka, the energetic Tomo, the short-tempered Yomi, the quiet, reserved Sakaki, and the competitive, eccentric Kagura.

Much of the show revolves around everyday moments, whether it's studying together, going on summer vacations, or simply finding new ways to annoy one another with all kinds of tomfoolery; these girls will always find a way to make you grin at the slightest bit of their lighthearted banter or actions.

And you see, watching this group become increasingly comfortable with one another throughout their high school journey makes their inevitable graduation feel incredibly bittersweet. It’s genuinely one of the shows my friends and I have come to adore, not because of its niche memes, but because there’s an actual heartwarming friendship here that grows with each episode.

#4209. Reinstated Aurora Gaming beat F9 EICAR to win Valorant Europe Qualifier 1

Aurora Gaming came from a map down to beat F9 EICAR 2-1 and win the first VCT EMEA Kickoff Europe open qualifier. The win came days after they were put back into the bracket when the UK team BONK was disqualified for cheating.

The VCT EMEA Kickoff: Europe Qualifier 2027 decider got under way at 18:45. The series began on Lotus. Aurora’s chiwa was named most valuable player of the series.

The Aurora roster lists Boo, chiwa, Derke, B1SK and trexx. F9 EICAR, based in France, fielded Kipperman, Destrian, Tenshi, izana and Geekkooo.

Aurora’s run nearly ended early. BONK, a UK Valorant roster, beat them 2-1 in the round of 32 on 6 November. That result followed a comeback from 3-11 down on Bind. Riot’s ruling against BONK reversed Aurora’s exit. Every BONK player and registered team member was provisionally suspended. Project 100K and ycatble returned to the bracket along with Aurora.

The qualifier left no room for error. It was a single-elimination bracket for 256 teams, and every match was a best-of-three. Once reinstated, Aurora did not drop a map before the final. They beat Pixel Lumina 2-0 in the second semi-final.

In the first semi-final, xXxMasterProMegaTeamxXx fell 2-1 to F9 EICAR. The French side had arrived at the qualifier in mixed form. F9 EICAR lost 0-2 to WIP Esports in VCL France: Revolution Stage 2 2026 and were twice beaten 1-2 by Mandatory. A 2-1 result against Esprit Shōnen was their only victory in that run.

The Elo power rankings show the gap on paper. F9 EICAR sit at rank 241, with a rating of 1405 and a 6-16 record in 22 rated matches. Aurora are unranked.

The final still carried weight. Seeding for the playoff stage would be decided by the result, Insider Gaming reported.

The stakes are clear. Under Riot’s 2027 system, four non-partner teams will reach VCT EMEA Kickoff. Two will come from Europe, one from Türkiye and one from the Middle East and North Africa.

— Aurora Valorant (@Aurora_Valorant) November 10, 2026

That leaves European hopefuls chasing places at a 12-team LAN event. VCT 2027 EMEA Kickoff will be run by Riot Games at the Riot Games Arena in Berlin.

The playoff field is not yet complete. The top four teams from each open qualifier move on, and the second Europe open qualifier is set for 12 to 15 November. The playoffs will use a modified double-elimination bracket of best-of-three matches, with a best-of-five grand final. The top two finishers earn places at VCT 2027 EMEA Kickoff, whose window runs from 14 January to 7 February.

#4208. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

In Bloom, players will be able to find maps that reveal caves that you can send your Pikmin into to battle and find treasure. You can also find maps for Bloom by playing Pikmin 4. #4206. GTA Features That Made Each Game Feel Completely Different

Usama Mehmood is a Senior Writer at DualShockers with more than five years of experience in the video game industry. He has been writing professionally since 2021 and covering games since 2022, with work spanning guides, lists, reviews, and features across action-adventure games, JRPGs, open-world titles, racing games,

If there’s one thing you can appreciate about the GTA games, it's that Rockstar has constantly reinvented the franchise with almost every major entry. Sure, the core sandbox formula of stealing cars, causing mayhem, and getting into trouble with the cops has stayed largely the same. Still, the actual experience of playing these games has evolved heavily over the years.

From DMA Design to GTA III, GTA V, and RDR2, let's take a look back at how Rockstar Games changed open-world gaming and why GTA 6 has so much to live up to.

Having revisited some of these older entries over the years, I've come to appreciate just how much personality each game brings to the table. With GTA VI preparing to take the franchise into a whole other league of greatness, I thought it would be a good time to look back at the features that made each installment stand out.Note: We'll only be discussing the 3D and HD trilogy games, so six in total.

I recently got to talk about it in a feature piece as well that you should totally check out later, but no matter the repetitive mission design of GTA 3, you can’t argue against how it laid a technical foundation with its introduction of a fully 3D Open World that you can freely explore and interact with across two distinctive boroughs of Liberty City.

And if we’re talking a deeper comparison just for scale, this was genuinely the first time you could explore this relatively vast urban environment from street level, with NPC pedestrians and moving traffic. More importantly, missions no longer felt like isolated arcade challenges since you could approach the world at your own pace and cause trouble with total freedom.

While GTA 3 gave us a convincing metropolitan playground to cause mayhem in, Rockstar didn’t stop there: just a year later, we’d be transported to a fictionalized 1980s Miami in GTA Vice City. The neon lights, pastel-colored buildings, beaches, and culturally fitting soundtrack made the city feel like an entirely different world.

It’s not the most distinctive trait compared to other entries in the series, but it is hard to imagine the franchise without Vice City's influence, a game that ended up making its entire setting feel like a character in its own right. Plus, customizing Tommy in a variety of outfits while driving a Cheetah with MJ’s Billie Jean playing in the background is a definitive core memory for many players.

It’s an undisputed fact that GTA: San Andreas is one of the greatest sandbox games of all time, single-handedly the PlayStation 2’s best-selling game and one of the only games that pushed the console to its absolute limit. I mean that quite literally, because you had this enormous map at the time, and the madmen at Rockstar used every fragment of the PS2’s memory to render it for the player.

Surprisingly, that wasn’t even the game's standout feature. You see, GTA San Andreas took personalization to another level by letting you shape CJ into the kind of protagonist you wanted. Think of light-hearted RPG elements.

Eating too much could make him gain weight, while working out at the gym could help him build muscle. There was also more to it than just looking different, though, because you could improve CJ’s stamina, driving, weapon proficiency, and other stats through regular gameplay activities or certain actions.

And the cherry on top was that you could also experiment with various hairstyles, clothing, tattoos, and even fighting styles. To me (and arguably for many others), this game is still one of the most ambitious releases ever and a personal childhood favorite that I’ve completed more than a dozen times.

Take-Two has had an absolutely killer Q2, leading them to feed GTA fever more and more.

We’re officially moving into the HD Trilogy, and after three games built around this arcade-style gameplay foundation, GTA IV took a whole new and different direction. Rockstar wanted their near-identical NYC Liberty City to feel as grounded as possible, and that passion extended beyond its darker narrative and more realistic presentation stuff, like the driving model.

That’s because GTA IV marked a huge technological leap for Rockstar, mainly because it was the first GTA game built using the studio's RAGE engine (Rockstar Advanced Game Engine). That was the blueprint, bringing together systems for rendering, physics, animation, audio, and more. However, what really brought it all together was Rockstar incorporating NaturalMotion's Euphoria technology.

Euphoria is a procedural animation system that allowed characters to react dynamically to their surroundings instead of relying entirely on predetermined animations. So take, for instance, shooting someone in the leg, knocking a pedestrian over, or sending Niko flying through a windshield during a car crash, and their reactions could differ depending on the smallest of circumstances.

It gave GTA IV’s physics such an unparalleled sense of speciality for me that it was almost difficult to wholeheartedly appreciate this feature at that time unless you really went ham on the chaos or noticed the finer details during gameplay.

So the funny story for 13-year-old me was how not being up to date with the gaming stratosphere at the time led me to be jaw-dropped that GTA 5 was already releasing worldwide… and then that jaw kept staying on the floor with how starstruck I was left, being transported back to this ginormous reimagination of Los Santos, one that would keep me company for the next decade.

However, instead of following a single criminal throughout the entire adventure, Rockstar tried a completely different storytelling approach here: three playable protagonists. You could switch between Michael, Franklin, and Trevor, letting you experience Los Santos through three very different perspectives. Someone might say the OG GTAs did the multiple-protagonist thing, but that’s not even the point.

You could switch characters between certain missions; some even made it mandatory to do so to facilitate the ongoing set piece or gameplay mechanic. It also made things interesting outside the missions as well because you could seamlessly switch between characters to find them engaged in their own day-to-day routine or unexpected/bizarre moments, and yes, that’s meant exactly for Trevor.

Yeah, yeah, I know, the game’s not even out yet. However, from everything Rockstar has shown us so far, Jason and Lucia's relationship already feels like one of the franchise's most noteworthy additions. Unlike GTA V, where the three protagonists mostly had separate lives and storylines, GTA VI puts far more emphasis on the bond between its two central characters. You can do the usual hangout stuff, like going out for a drink, playing pool, kayaking, or even pulling off robberies, but it goes beyond that because you can reply to texts or answer phone calls to further grow the relationship. It sounds simple, but I know there will be plenty of hidden details and intricacies in typical Rockstar fashion.

I also love that Rockstar isn't forcing you down the romantic route, since these two will remain partners in crime no matter how much you choose to nurture their relationship throughout each mission and the story, but those who put in the effort will have more opportunities to experience that side of their lives. In fact, I’d honestly rather try to ruin their relationship in a second playthrough, if possible, just to see the different outcomes or details.

GTA VI will be one of the biggest video game releases in our lifetimes, and it will be talked about for years to come.

#4204. The Sims developer vows "our values are unchanged," as it teases multiple projects from post-Saudi-owned EA

The team behind one of EA's most diverse franchises has issued a statement about its future under the soon-to-be Saudi-owned publisher.

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.)

Some of these projects will see more playtesting throughout 2026, so you should probably sign up for The Sims Labs if you want to hear about when/how you can get involved.

#4200. GTA 6 Cheat Codes Are Already Out There, And Here’s All of Them

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

The wait for Grand Theft Auto 6 is almost over. Rockstar's long-awaited open-world adventure launches on November 19, and the first reviews are already rolling in, with the game currently sitting at a staggering 99 on Metacritic, tying the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the highest score in the site's history.

But while most players are still getting ready to explore Leonida for the first time, some fans are already thinking about a much more important part of the GTA experience: cheat codes. And, perhaps unsurprisingly, they are already circulating online!

According to GTA Base, a well-known resource among Grand Theft Auto fans, there are already 61 cheats cataloged for GTA 6. They cover everything from getting extra cash and spawning vehicles to changing the weather and applying bizarre visual filters. But there's one catch: you won't be able to use any of them until you finish the main story. So yes, Rockstar really wants you to earn your chaos this time.

Unlike previous entries, GTA 6 doesn't let you activate cheats right from the beginning. First, you need to complete the story, which unlocks the Cheats section under Progress Menu. Each cheat also has its own requirement, so simply knowing a button combination isn't enough.

Once you've unlocked the cheat you want, bring up your in-game phone, hold L1 + R1 on PlayStation 5 or LB + RB on Xbox Series X|S, and enter the corresponding combination using the D-pad. Interestingly, all the sequences use directional inputs, meaning the codes are identical on both platforms.

Unlike previous entries, GTA 6 doesn't let you activate cheats right from the beginning. First, you need to complete the story, which unlocks the Cheats section under Progress Menu.

One more thing before you start turning Vice City upside down: using cheats disables Trophies and Achievements, as well as the ability to save your game! So make sure you have a clean save before experimenting.

GTA Base just proved how quick they are and has already put together an impressive list of 61 cheats, organized into five categories. Not all of them have been fully discovered just yet, though, so some button combinations are still missing!

We've included everything known so far, along with what each cheat does and its code whenever it's been confirmed. We'll keep updating this article as more combinations pop up, so be sure to check back if you're planning to cause some trouble in Vice City.

Rockstar is known for putting insane levels of detail into their games, but here is how they are going above and beyond with GTA VI.

GTA VI will be one of the biggest video game releases in our lifetimes, and it will be talked about for years to come.

For the latest updates and any newly confirmed combinations, check out GTA Base's PS5 cheat guide and Xbox Series X|S cheat guide. With the game launching tomorrow, it probably won't take long for players to start uncovering the remaining codes. Just remember to finish the story first!

#4197. Battlefield 6 Season 2 delayed like many of us expected, but we're getting a new update and a bonus battle pass path

Battlefield 6 has pushed back its next season by nearly a month in order to refine Season 2 content and implement more of players' feedback.

Battlefield Studios has released its first official communication in 2026. Rather than unveil the second season of Battlefield 6, however, the developer instead announced a delay. The currently ongoing Season 1 was initially meant to end on Tuesday, January 20, hence why the developer had to communicate something this week.

Season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off. Given the current sentiment around the game, this news isn’t surprising in the least.

In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios said that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.

The developer did not offer any hints about Season 2, but there’s an incredibly brief teaser trailer featuring a soldier wearing a gas mask emerging from an environment drenched in toxic gas.

Given that Battlefield 6’s battle royale mode Redsec does not utilise the popular encroaching gas mechanic (using an encroaching ring of fire instead), it’s possible that we may be looking at something new in multiplayer akin to Battlefield 1. Of course, this may just be a visual piece that doesn’t reflect the gameplay of Season 2.

Escalating the fight with new threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj

What we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension update is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end. It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

Similar to other Bonus Paths, the new Frostfire Bonus Path can be completed alongside the Season 1 battle pass. You’ll need 110 Bonus Path Points in total if you want to earn everything it has to offer, with each tier requiring 10 points. It is worth noting, however, that Frostfire Points are only earned through weekly challenges, meaning there won’t be any bonus challenges associated with it.

Frostfire includes several new customisation rewards, of course, such as a Weapon Package, soldier skin, XP boosts and the usual run of unlocks.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.

#4196. T1 brings TenZ out of retirement a day after re-signing crashies from Fnatic

T1 has added two-time Masters champion Tyson 'TenZ' Ngo to its Valorant roster for VCT Pacific in 2027. The move ends his retirement and builds on T1's signing of crashies, who has just left London-based Fnatic.

T1 has ended Tyson ‘TenZ’ Ngo’s retirement. The organisation confirmed on 12 November that he will join its Valorant roster for VCT Pacific in 2027. It made the announcement with a post and a welcome video.

T1 called him a ‘living legend’ of Valorant. It said he was starting a new chapter with the organisation.

TenZ retired from professional play in 2024. He has spent this year at T1 as a content creator. The announcement moves him from that role into the competitive squad.

His record explains the attention. With Sentinels, he beat Fnatic 3-0 in the Masters Reykjavík 2021 final. He then won Masters Madrid 2024 with a 3-2 win over Gen.G. That made him the first Americas player to win more than one VCT Masters event, Liquipedia records.

The TenZ news came a day after T1 confirmed Austin ‘crashies’ Roberts. He returns six years after T1 released him in September 2020. crashies called T1 the place ‘where it all started’. He said he was excited for the new challenge.

He played for Fnatic from 11 December 2024 until 4 November 2026. He joined T1 on 11 November 2026.

His exit is part of a wider reshuffle at the London-based organisation. Fnatic lost the Masters Toronto 2025 grand final 3-1 to Paper Rex. It then lost the Valorant Champions 2025 grand final in Paris 3-2 to NRG. On 2 November, Fnatic released head coach Andrey ‘ENGH’ Sholokhov. It said it was making changes ahead of the 2027 season.

T1 has also kept some continuity. It extended BuZz’s contract on 6 November 2026. The new deal runs until the end of 2028.

The VCT structure for 2027 was announced on 28 October. Under it, the eight Pacific partner teams go straight into Kickoff in January 2027. The other four Kickoff places go to teams from regional open qualifiers.

The KING is back! 👑A living legend of VALORANT, 'TenZ' begins a new chapter with T1.Ready to make history under the red wings, join us in giving him a warm welcome!

📺 https://t.co/ny3VtTtYnx#T1VALORANT pic.twitter.com/gmgLEzXJR2

Before Kickoff, T1 has a date in Los Angeles. It is one of six teams directly invited to Red Bull Home Ground 2026. Fnatic, Sentinels, G2 Esports, NRG and ZETA DIVISION have also been invited. That puts the former clubs of both TenZ and crashies in the same field as T1.

The event runs from 10 to 13 December. Group stage matches are on 10 and 11 December. Bracket play and the semi-finals follow on 12 December. The grand final is on 13 December.

The headline tells the story: The Elder Scrolls VI has an official subtitle and it's Sentinel. So the full game is now titled The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, or, as we will undoubtedly refer to it moving forward, as we colloquially do with the previous three games (Morrowind, Oblivion, and Skyrim), Sentinel.

The news comes from Bethesda's various social media accounts, which are all sharing the video above. Along with the video, music, and the title, it also shares the text as a quote attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest to High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell (4E 206): "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate."

Sentinel is one of the nine major kingdoms within Hammerfell and is the capital of both the Alik'r Desert region and the Myrkwasa region of the Alik'r (source: elderscrolls.fandom). With this knowledge, it's fair to assume Sentinel will have many desert locations.

The name continues the tradition of naming the games after locations in the Elder Scrolls universe. Oblivion is the sort of exception, as it is a realm, but it still counts. We still don't know exactly when The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel will be released, but we're now about seven years from its original announcement at E3 2018.

The higher a hero's rarity, the more troops can join them in battle (SSR heroes can take a lot more troops than R heroes).

If you want to learn more about the game, make sure you check out our other Top War articles!

Maximo - A powerful hero that will greatly enhance any air force units and can quite literally change the entire course of a battle. He's a premium hero who is worth investing in, and by all means, one who can work on the offensive and defensive front.

Selina - She's a good hero thanks to the amazing buffs she provides, and if you manage to max her out, she greatly increases the maximum HP of other units, as well as their attack. Serval - Another broken premium hero that can make life a living hell for enemies. She's especially good when paired up with some of the other top-tier heroes, since they can stack their stats.

Preycis - This Army hero is great for aiming at the back-row enemies and is one of the best at specialising in that. #4192. Rockstar President Breaks Silence Ahead of GTA 6 Launch

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

Given the mad fervor with which the universe as we know it is preparing for the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 tomorrow, I don’t think it’d be hyperbolic to call Rockstar the, er, rockstar of video game development. Even if its games take a hot minute to come out, they’re always bangers when they do, and both the industry and the gaming public naturally hang upon their every word in a manner not dissimilar to someone like Mick Jagger.

Even so, not everyone who works at Rockstar is the kind of person who seeks out the public eye. Take, for example, Sam Houser, who is both the president of Rockstar and the executive producer of GTA 6. Houser has worked on the GTA series in some capacity since its very first title in 1997, but unlike some of the company’s more front-facing divisions and employees, he has always had a tendency to keep his head down and just let the games speak for themselves.

However, with such a major landmark title like GTA 6 quite literally on the horizon, the president of the company bringing it is at least informally obligated to share a few words, and that’s exactly what Houser did in a brief, yet poignant statement shared with IGN.

Players already have a list of 61 cheats to look forward to.

As Houser explained to IGN, the predominant belief that spurs Rockstar’s developmental ethos forward is that games can be just as poignant of a medium of storytelling as any other, whether it be film, television, or print. Not only that, but games, in their ideal form, can become a vital component of the modern cultural zeitgeist and give rise to settings and characters that stick with us long after the fact.

This firm belief has culminated in the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 after 13 long years of development. “While things have changed and time has passed, one aspect holds true: We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special,” Houser said.

He added that, whether someone is experiencing the GTA series for the first time or has been with it since the very beginning, the game’s world and the narrative contained within it is meant to be shaped by player interaction.

We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of.

“We hope it felt both familiar and entirely new, and above all, we hope that you had fun. We are incredibly grateful to you and everything that you do to celebrate games. We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you,” Houser concluded with a word of thanks.

Obviously, every professional game developer out there wants their product to be well-received, both so it makes back the money invested into it, and so that it really sticks with the players who experienced it. Grand Theft Auto 6 may not technically be out yet, but even ahead of release proper, I’d say it’s well on track to meeting and exceeding Houser’s hopes.

For one thing, just this morning, the embargo officially broke on the game’s critical reviews, and perhaps unsurprisingly, GTA 6 has received the official seal of being the hottest thing since toasted bread, both from our own Steve Hannley and pretty much everyone else. Its Metacritic reviewer average has reached 99, tying it with one of the most highly-reviewed games of all time, the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which is kind of amusing considering the remake of that game just came out.

As for cash, well, it’s difficult to say for certain without hard numbers, but pre-release projections had the game netting its publisher, Take-Two Interactive, a stunning $3.5 billion in revenue, and considering the number of people planning on skipping work to play on launch day, I’d say that’s a fairly realistic figure.

#4191. Afterwords – Marvel’s Wolverine

We interviewed game director Mike Daly after the launch of Insomniac’s recent Wolverine game to get his take on what makes Wolverine and Spidey different to work on, his thoughts on breadcrumb trails, and why Logan can’t ever seem to get the girl.

Insomniac had extensive experience working on well-known superhero characters before starting on Wolverine. Early on, what traits or qualities of Logan as a story character and playable avatar did you know you wanted to focus on, distinct from the Spider-Man games and character?

From a story perspective, we wanted Logan to be a man with centuries of experiences that he can’t remember, creating a mix of being worn, wizened, and cynical. His resilience makes him fearless, which comes through in his candid manner, and he can’t ignore his sense of justice, as much as he would like to.

For gameplay, it was important that players felt the difference made by his healing factor, claws, berserker rage, animalistic strength, enhanced senses, his adamantium skeleton, and corresponding weight.

In both story and gameplay, emotionally and physically, Wolverine is a hero who gets hurt and feels that pain deeply but always gets back up again and presses on. This dogged resilience was really important to us and a central theme of story and gameplay.

Wolverine is more of a linear adventure than the open-world exploration of a big city seen in Spidey. In my playthrough, that added to the sense of relentless pacing that characterizes Wolverine as a fictional lead. Was that part of the thinking behind why the game was built that way, or was the more linear path there for other reasons?

Ultimately, we made a game suited for a Wolverine story that had comic book pacing – action and meaningful story development on every page.

We experimented with different structures and stories, evaluating from the perspective of: “Is this the best way to do Wolverine justice?” As the various things we tried didn’t feel right, we had to challenge our assumptions and look to our favorite Wolverine stories for inspiration, which led us to where we ended up – a story with momentum in which every beat felt authentic to the character.

Scenes and gameplay sequences that might have been fine in other games but didn’t strongly evoke Wolverine undermined the consistency of the fantasy we were trying to create, so we tried to keep things very focused.

After the game’s release, there was an active online conversation about some of the breadcrumb-trail guidance the game offers to lead you to pickups, or to mark the continued golden path of progression. What was the thinking internally about that design decision, and your take on the debate after the game launched?

Our thinking was that it was essential to make the player feel like they were empowered by Logan’s enhanced senses, a canonical mutant ability, enabling players to do things they could not with other characters. We wanted to weave that power into as many parts of the game as we could, so that if Logan could smell or hear something relevant, the player could see it too.

For collectibles, we wanted players to enjoy seeking out and spotting senses cues, enabling you to find things that would have been obscure to other characters. Using the cues, players can cover a lot of ground without feeling the need to scour, maintaining story and action momentum.

After the game launched, we saw feedback from players that interpreted senses as abstract designer guidance, along with a desire for options in how they approached exploration and discovery. Fortunately, we have been able to incorporate this feedback from players in our post-launch patches. One aspect we’ve improved is the scent trail’s organic presentation, so they give a stronger impression that they belong in the world rather than being an abstraction. For players that want to do more manual exploration, we’ve added options to remove the sense cues for optional collectibles, and one to make scent trails dimmer until the player requests a hint.

Ultimately, enhanced senses are still essential to creating an authentic Wolverine, and that’s still reflected in the cinematic and environmental storytelling of the game. I think it’s great that on top of that, players now have more flexibility in how they experience them.

As a longtime comics fan, I found Logan’s combat system especially exciting, particularly for the relentless forward momentum it provided. What do you think were some of the keys to nailing that dynamic, as distinct from other high-quality third-person action games?

There were a few key elements we wanted to get right - Logan’s resilience, rage, claw feel, and overall lethality.

For resilience, Logan’s healing factor needed to feel important for survival - a prominent element of the system. A natural starting point there was to try continual regeneration so you could outlast enemies, but that quickly fell apart as it incentivized the player to slow the pace of combat or even retreat for maximum advantage. Even though it was incredibly effective at enabling survival, it was also hard to notice by the player so it didn’t feel prominent.

The key to solving this problem was making a connection between rage and healing factor. The Last Stand mechanic is a healing surge that can happen when you lose all your health, themed as using adrenaline to keep Logan’s heart beating. This incentivized aggression and made a space for an up-close look at visceral healing.

Speaking of rage, it’s the backbone of the combat system where being an indicator of momentum is key. At the low end of rage, you don’t have the safety net of Last Stand, so your decision-making naturally biases towards survival; ensuring you prioritize threat assessment and defense. As you climb into the middle tier, you have the leeway to push your luck for longer combos or barrages that let you build up rage and get kills faster. Finally, you get to rage tier 3, where the quick decay of rage makes your rate of kills the top priority, so you might prefer to attack groups over ranged stragglers just for the improved kill density. Beyond the mechanics, we change the presentation of combat, especially through Logan’s animations and exertion to reflect his state of mind. The presentation and systemic incentives drive the player into a frenzy, just like Wolverine.

We invested a lot in the details of claw feel to make sure it was distinct from general game attacks. Claws shred, so we added locational body damage to our enemies to reflect that, along with a dynamic blood system where it globs together as it is spilled, splatters on contact with characters or the environment, drips down the walls, diffuses in the water, and other details. Many kills throughout combat are punctuated with custom animations with cinematic camera work that pushes in and frames the puncturing of claws into the body for a strong impression of the connection and weight of the puncture. Severing limbs on these attacks is an occasional reminder of how sharp Logan’s adamantium claws are. Reinforcing this is top-notch sound and haptics design, so each hit registers.

The last aspect I’ll touch on is lethality, the rate at which Wolverine is able to dispatch enemies and vice versa. We found that fights where enemies were more technical and could survive a lot undermined what players expected to experience as Wolverine, which was aggressively and lethally tearing through a lot of enemies. On the other hand, combat was less exciting if the enemies didn’t feel like a serious and deadly threat, and you didn’t feel like Wolverine if a little bit of caution could enable you to defend perfectly and avoid all damage.

These aspects led us towards encounters where you confronted large groups of enemies that were highly aggressive, to the point of feeling unfair. Enemies can’t believably go toe-to-toe with Wolverine alone, even world-class mercenaries, so their strategy is in group coordination, which creates a counterweight to Wolverine’s own rage-based momentum.

Marvel’s Wolverine draws in a number of characters from across the X-Men comic mythology, but notably makes no mention of some foundational figures of that fiction – Professor Xavier and Magneto. That, in turn, leads to dramatically different lives for characters like Jean Grey or Logan. Is the narrative you crafted an intentional exploration of a world where those figures weren’t present in the early days of mutant emergence?

I would say it was more of an exploration of the character than the world. We wanted a story where Logan is pulled into conflict not because he’s a crusader, but because there’s no other option. There are no X-Men to help. His growth as a person should be a challenging journey, which could go unearned if he was surrounded by wise, supportive, heroic characters pushing him in the right direction. In contrast, his dynamic with the members of Team X evokes his struggle. The adversity to personal growth is what makes it interesting.

Jean does end up being the person that pushes him in the right direction, and that works because they can relate to each other, having had similar struggles.

In several versions of Marvel storytelling, Jean and Logan share a special bond, but Jean ultimately chooses Scott Summers as a partner. But even without that barrier in your story, Logan still hits some roadblocks to love. Is Wolverine fundamentally a better character when he just can’t get the girl?

The way I would put it is that a Wolverine story is fundamentally better when you empathize with Logan’s pain and admire him for pressing on despite it. That goes for his emotional pain as much as physical. He’s a tragic character in this regard – all he wants is to be at peace but can never find it for long.

Wolverine gets to take on a lot of the “heavy hitters” of his comic mythology in different boss fights throughout the game. When you began development, do you recall who the very first character was that you decided he simply had to fight in your game?

Sabretooth. No character is a better foil for Logan. His inner turmoil and chaotic behavior helps illustrate Logan’s own inner beast and his struggle to resist it. Sabretooth’s strength and mutant powers also provide a mirror to Logan in combat, and his savagery creates shocking moments that leave an impression. We knew an epic confrontation with Sabretooth was going to be a thing from the start.

#4190. Dota 2 returns to Esports World Cup 2027 as PARIVISION chase a first repeat title

Dota 2 will return to the Riyadh-hosted Esports World Cup in 2027, though dates, format and prize money are still to come. The title has never been won twice, and its prize pool has fallen at every edition so far.

Dota 2’s place at Esports World Cup 2027 was announced without dates, a prize pool, a format or any invited teams. The whole event is listed for July to August 2027.

The 2026 tournament had originally been planned for Riyadh before it was moved to Paris on 20 May 2026.

The first edition, Riyadh Masters 2024, carried a US$5,000,000 prize pool. In 2025 Team Spirit took US$1,000,000 from a US$3,000,000 pool in a 16-team event. The 2026 tournament ran from 7 to 19 July with 24 teams. That field was eight teams larger than a year earlier.

The winner still takes a large share. PARIVISION collected US$750,000, or 37.5% of the pool, plus 1,000 Club Championship points. Runners-up BetBoom Team received US$340,000 and 750 points, Liquipedia reported.

Those points feed into a larger prize. In 2026 the Club Championship paid US$30 million across the top 24 clubs. The champion club received US$7 million from an overall event prize pool of US$75 million. AG.AL won it with 5,300 points, stopping Team Falcons from winning a third title in a row. For organisations weighing the cost of a Dota 2 roster, that club prize is part of the calculation.

Not every club is staying. Falcons released all five players from the roster that won The International 2025, according to Timesaver.gg.

No club or player has won the event’s Dota 2 title more than once. Each of the three editions went to a different club with a different roster. Gaimin Gladiators beat Team Liquid in the 2024 final. A year later, Team Spirit swept Team Falcons 3-0. As the 2026 champions, PARIVISION now get the first chance to defend the title.

PVISION are your Dota 2 at EWC26 Champions! 👏 pic.twitter.com/34U67Oaj7G

— Esports World Cup (@EWC_EN) July 20, 2026

Their rivals arrive in form. Team Spirit went out of the 2026 event before the final. A month later, they won The International 2026 in Shanghai. Yatoro and Collapse became the first players to win three Internationals. Team Yandex finished third at both the 2026 Esports World Cup and The International. After signing ATF, they won PGL Wallachia Season 9 and BLAST SLAM VIII.

The route into the event is taking shape. The organiser’s Road to EWC qualifier programme for 2027 aims to involve 1.8 million players across more than 400 events. Qualifier slots for each game will be announced later. Counter-Strike 2, already confirmed for both 2027 and 2028, will hold a 32-team event in Riyadh from 20 July to 1 August 2027.

#4189. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

Mac, PC, PS4, PS5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S

#4188. The fastest cars in CSR Racing 2, in every tier

Updated with the very best cars to race in 2026

Updated on November 18th, 2026 - Version: 6.7.2

Want to quickly compare stats on all the cars in CSR Racing 2? Then this is the guide for you.

Below, we've listed all the base stats for every car and highlighted which wins in each category. R stands for Rep Bonus, and F is for Fusion Slots.

Obviously, every car can be completely changed through upgrades and tuning, but these starting numbers give you a good indication of that car's overall abilities. It provides a quick glimpse at the stats, which might just be enough to help you pick out which car to choose to purchase next.

We've also included some thoughts on which are the best cars in CSR Racing 2 - both rare imports and those you can buy with in-game cash.

Just click through below to find out the fastest cars in every tier.

Many great choices in this category. At first glance, it seems like the Golf GTI MK1 is a clear winner, especially as it also has a 6% RP bonus and eight fusion slots. However, it must be won in the Rare Imports lot, which means it's a lot harder to come by.

On top of that, the fastest car so far is the Ford Mustang Boss 302 with e.c level 50, which means, even though it's not as fast early on, it can make it up in the later stages.

The Veloster Turbo R Spec is also a decent choice, but can only be purchased with (150) Gold.

The M235i Coupe is a fantastic car for Tier 2, especially since you can buy it for just $75,000. It's light and has high power, but you'll need to upgrade your tyres to bring the grip up.

Potentially, the Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Coupe can be the fastest in this tier and by quite a big margin. Not early on, though. The same goes for the Ferrari 250 GTO and Aston Martin DB5.

If you want Tier 2's best vehicle, you'll need to earn the F-150 from the Rare Imports lot.

The Ferrari California 30 is obviously still one of the best Tier 3 cars in class - no wonder it's being kept back as a prize.

So if you can't win that, the SRT Hellcat at 825 G is a good choice with its high power, low shift time, and strong grip. If you only have dollars to spend, get the RS 5 Coupe.

At level 50, the Pontiac GTO "The Judge" is the fastest car in this category. The BMW M2 (G87) Coupe "M Performance" is right behind it in second place. As you would expect, any variant of the Civic Type R is going to be fast! This is one of my favourite categories, as there are several good choices.

The GT-R (R35) Premium looks like a pretty good vehicle for this tier. Not only is it affordable, but it has an amazing grip (too much, perhaps?!) and a low shift time. You'll need to work on power and lowering the weight with a lighter body.

The Viper ACR is another good option: it has great power for the tier, a low shift time, and 23 Fusion Slots.

Right now, the Rocket Bunny is looking more attractive than ever, but the big Grand Cherokee Trackhawk is tempting too.

At this point, the game has some amazing cars to use, and the latest releases push performance to the limits. These are by far the fastest cars in CSR Racing 2. The Bugatti Chiron is a fantastic choice, as is the FXX K, but launch cars such as the Bugatti Veyron and One:1 are still great.

If you don't want to rely on Rare Import lot wins, the Aventador LP 700-4 is a good bet with its high power, strong grip, and its relatively lightweight to boot.

Regardless, though, there's no doubt you'll have fun with vehicles like the 'Cuda "TorC" in CSR2.
