#4187. Holiday Gift Guide 2026

With the holiday gift-giving season upon us, it’s time to think about the gaming fans in your life and find the ideal present to brighten their day. And if you’re the gamer in the family, we always encourage you to circle relevant items in the coming pages and leave your magazine open in hard-to-miss locations around the house. We’ve scoured dozens of tech products, tabletop games, collectibles, and more to select and highlight some of the coolest items we found this year.

We recommended the Board shortly after its launch, but with its expanded game library and lower price than first-adopter rates, this holiday season is an ideal time to make the leap. This family-friendly platform features original games that sit comfortably between the digital and physical divide. The horizontally placed screen shows the backdrop of one of the several included games, or the sold-separately add-on games that have popped in since launch. Each game has its own real physical play pieces that interact with the action onscreen, often in innovative and charming ways. Think of it as the best of both worlds between board games and video games, and you’ll get what they’re shooting for here. $399

Few additions to the latest Dungeons & Dragons rules pack as much punch and value as this new expansion, focusing on ways to develop further and evolve the use of magic across your tabletop gaming sessions. New subclasses, spells, creatures, magical items, and factions add thoughtful, intriguing options for both players looking to play someone new and DMs hunting for new story hooks and challenges. $50

If you’re as excited as we are about this month’s celebration of the Tomb Raider legacy (see p. 40), this centerpiece statue is an ideal fit for your collection. Standing roughly nine inches in height, Lara is poised for exploration in her original classic garb. The sculpt strikes a perfect balance between crisp detail and stylistic presentation, in line with that early version of the character; the metallic blue motorcycle paint is especially striking. $250

For players longing for the glory days of stand-up arcade games, it’s hard to beat Arcade 1Up’s approach. The team’s sturdy cabinets look and sound great as a marquee feature of your game room. The new Outrun machine features much of the original display art, a bright 19-inch screen, and responsive gas and brake pedals as you steer around those tight corners. Sega has packed in OutRun, Turbo OutRun, OutRunners, and Power Drift. If old-school racing isn’t your thing, look for cabinets that run the gamut from Pac-Man to Joust to Claw Machines. $629.99

The long-running Nendoroid figures continue to be an attractive but still affordable choice for building collections across numerous fan-favorite series. There are somewhere around 2000 characters at this point! New entries like the Genshin Impact collection make a strong case for the line. The look is chibi, the quality is excellent, poseability is high, and customizable face and accessory parts let you change up your display over time. $46

We’ve previously sung the praises of Libernovo’s versatile approach to an ergonomic gaming chair, which includes a lumbar stretch functionality, a steady recline option for comfortable pushback without sudden shifts, and dynamically adjusting parts as you move through your day. The Maxis line does all that, but addresses one of the fundamental problems for at least some users with the original – it wasn’t big enough. With features like a wider base and longer headrest reach, the Maxis aims to provide the same comfort to the players who are tall or wide enough to need the extra breathing room. $1119

If you’re the player on your team who likes to have easy access to soundboards and real-time voice changing, the Key Pocket could be just the ticket. This small device straps onto your phone for mobile play, but it’s also compatible with consoles, Discord, Twitch, or just about any place you want to tweak audio on the fly. A free tier gives you access to some voice-changing and sounds, while a separate subscription opens up hundreds of thousands of additional options. But be warned: we can’t help you after your friends abandon you for that baby voice you won’t stop using. $99

The question of the best bang for your buck in modern consoles has become extraordinarily complicated, especially as tech prices have soared in recent years. There’s no right answer, but Sony’s high-end machine walks the line of offering extremely high-tier performance without escalating to even higher-priced gaming PCs. Higher and more consistent frame rates than on standard PS5, advanced ray tracing, and an increasing number of games that feature enhanced PSSR image options all add up to a better gaming experience, if you’re ready to make the significant price jump. $900

If the gamer in your life is looking for a stylish, understated way to express their love of the hobby, Anicorn’s designer watch collaboration with PlayStation could be a standout option. Available in black and a slick silver/white combo, the minimalist timepiece includes the familiar face buttons of Sony’s controller encased in an oil-injection display so they slowly and freely float across the watch as you move. $250

It’s a safe bet you’ve at least seen the popular Shashibo puzzle cubes by this point. We’ve been fans of their brain-teasing, fidgety fun for some time. Battle Shapes takes the core concept – reshaping the box into various distinct magnetically-locked shapes – and extends it into a timed game experience, playable solo or head-to-head. By targeting specific shapes, you significantly improve your speed with the toy, and scannable QR codes on the cards offer clear tutorials for each shape so you can prep for competition. $50

While the vast majority of gamers looking for good personal audio are going to be okay with a larger set of cans over their ears, We know more than a few players for whom that’s a definite no – for comfort, awareness of surrounding sounds, or other reasons. The Arc 5 earbuds aim to solve for that, with an over-ear design that feels extremely comfortable. And because they sit on the ear, you can still hear what’s going on around you. While that limits some aspects of the final sound quality, the inclusion of THX certification, Dolby Atmos optimization, and Dynamic Bass Enhancement helps to ensure audio is still very strong. $230

Across Lego’s many recent themes, Tolkien’s legendarium has offered some stellar sets. The largest yet is the capital of Gondor, with an astonishing 8,278 pieces and a height of roughly two feet. The castle/city build is impressive, featuring tons of interesting angles and turns. The finished product aims to offer the best of both worlds in presentation – a microscale representation of the front façade and a reverse minifigure-scale Hall of Kings. We especially like the inclusion of Denethor’s cherry tomatoes. $650

The original Azul is often cited as a foundational entry in modern board gaming. The “Kids” versions of celebrated titles aren’t always a sure bet, but this one holds up to scrutiny. Azul Kids lowers the complexity threshold but keeps the foundational strategic thinking. Players lay out uniquely shaped tiles into mosaic frameworks in colorful, appealing patterns; the basic concept of the original inspiration is clear, and kids as young as five can grasp and enjoy the fun. $25

Many corners of the collecting world have embraced the fun (and frequent despair) of blind boxes, where you never know exactly who you’ll get in a given series. Funism has a strong track record for quality, offering adorable smaller figures like their latest line of Evangelion collectibles. Each figure stands nearly four inches and features both human characters and mecha. You can buy singles and roll the dice, or purchase larger sets with a no-duplicates guarantee, which can save a lot of heartache if you’re trying to line your whole shelf. $21

If you’re going to spring for a high-end keyboard for PC gaming, it’s important that you like the feel of the keys. The slightly smaller overall 75% size profile of this Blackwidow has no impact on the great feel of typing – a clear highlight for the unit. The customizable, colored backlights are also a big selling point, as is the side command dial and built-in OLED display, which can be tweaked to show PC performance, GIFs, lighting brightness, and more. It’s a strong contender in a crowded field, and justifies its price with both comfort and customizability. $300

Beautiful, vibrant art and a refreshing take on the classic area-control board game genre are the two strongest reasons to take a close look at Wroth. Players control one of five races vying for supremacy across a conflict-ridden peninsula. Factions are asymmetric, so everyone has unique capabilities, and that adds significant replayability. Players roll and draft dice, allowing distinct actions that move the game forward. And move it does; unlike many games of this ilk, Wroth can be learned quickly and played to completion in a little over an hour. $65

Console and computer hardware prices are skyrocketing with no sign of slowing, and perhaps as a result, retro gaming handhelds are gaining popularity. Many quality devices are available, but what sets the Evercade Nexus apart is its officially licensed game cartridges. Imagine the nostalgic joy of a Game Boy, but with a cartridge that includes both Banjo-Kazooie and Tooie. The cartridge boxes even include manuals. For fans of physical media, Evercade Nexus is a great option. $199

This tiny USB-C plug-in (with included USB-A adapter) solves a bunch of audio challenges in one uniform device. It offers high-resolution Bluetooth transmission on iPhone, high-bitrate audio transmission to compatible LDAC headphones, enables high-quality Bluetooth output from your PC, and even low-latency Bluetooth audio on PS5 and Switch. In short, it takes a huge number of products with a USB port and ensures a dynamic Bluetooth audio connection with relative ease. $99

The original MV6 is a familiar sight on streams thanks to its clear voice reproduction and overall ease of use. Shure has built on that success with the Gen 2, offering an excellent standalone mic that doesn’t break the bank. Available in black or white, the Gen 2 features a handy auto-level mode that keeps volume even as you adjust your own amplitude, an adjustable denoiser for your space, a longer cable for out-of-the-box convenience, and three presets for plug-and-play use. In short, it’s an excellent choice if you want great performance without needing an audio engineering degree. $169

XR Glasses are still fighting for awareness, but once you try them, it’s easy to see why the concept is on the rise. Viture’s Pro 2 makes an impressive case for adoption, with a competitive price point, comfortable wear, and a giant 146-inch screen that floats in front of your face for gaming or work on your PC or phone. The display is crisp, bright, and impressive, even as the glasses are light and easy to use. With a mobile dock mini (sold separately), you can even snap onto a Switch 2 with ease and start playing instantly. $299

Role-playing gamers have several excellent universal systems to pick between when considering a story or campaign idea that might fall outside traditional genre staples. Among many good options, Cypher stands out as one of the very best. The system uses a rules-light, narrative-focused approach that prioritizes player-driven storytelling across everything from hard sci-fi to superheroes to intrigue- driven espionage. This is the corebook that’s needed to run and play the full system; additional books only add options. $50

As gamers have continually migrated toward personal audio that can rock amazing sound without disturbing the whole house, high-end premium headphones have become a dangerously competitive space. Turtle Beach meets that challenge head-on, with a robust option that sounds beautiful in use. The Stealth Pro II boasts the slick ability to wirelessly switch between different devices, which is awesome if you’re one of those players who regularly jumps between platforms to play your favorite titles. Like the whole category, it’s a lot to spend on a headset, but Dolby Atmos, active noise cancellation, and 60mm dual drivers all add up to a powerful argument. $300

With an increasing number of top-tier console and PC games like Resident Evil Village, No Man’s Sky, and Dead Cells now available on iOS, not to mention the consistent quality of Apple Arcade, Apple phones remain the best mobile platform for gaming. The 18 Pro Max phone has implemented a number of tweaks that strengthen the platform, including higher memory, much faster graphics processing, impressive HDR performance, and notably improved battery life, all adding up to a gaming experience that is working hard to justify your playtime when away from home. Starting at $1299

SteelSeries is best known for its strong audio line-up, but its push into premium-tier controllers exhibits a similar flair for quality and usability. The new Aeon Pro has a lot to recommend it as your go-to Xbox, PC, or mobile choice. The two included batteries (one of which can always be charging in the dock) ensure essentially unlimited playtime. The full-pull or hair triggers and buttons are clicky and satisfying, and the Hall Effect thumbsticks are built to minimize any drift. Textured handgrips and overall heft are ideal. And an onboard OLED lets you adjust profiles and button assignments, switch between platforms, and check battery at a glance. $260

Valve’s pricey VR headset isn’t a revolution in the medium, but the company has been invested in the technology since its inception. As a result, the Steam Frame is a very good, very comfortable headset. Like its competition, the Quest, its best use is playing games locally on the headset, and Steam’s library is vast and interesting. Wireless connected play to a powerful PC is also well done, but currently the included Wireless Adapter is not fully compatible with the Steam Machine – a baffling limitation we were shocked to confirm. VR is an expensive sub-hobby within video games, but Steam Frame is among the best ways to explore and enjoy it. $1059

#4185. 10 Changes You Might Not Have Noticed in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is pretty amazing. The team didn’t mess around, and instead changed many aspects of this beloved Nintendo 64 title. It has updated graphics, slightly altered story beats, and more. Of course, since the team rebuilt Hyrule, that means they could make a few changes. Castle Town is now much more detailed, and even Death Mountain’s layout changed slightly.

These are just some of the big changes, however, as Nintendo made a lot more changes, and some of them you might not even have noticed since they are so small. Despite being small, these changes are just as important as the large ones, as they make the game feel more complete.

This is a very small change that you might not have realized was made between the original game and the remake, and that is that the merchants actually move. While some of the shop owners had animation before, they typically just looked at Link.

While playing the remake, you will see that each merchant is now far more animated, but the big difference is that they will actually turn their head to look at the item you are buying from them. While this change wasn’t needed, it definitely makes the shop owners feel more alive rather than watching them stand there.

Have you ever been to Castle Town at night in the original Ocarina of Time? No? Well, that is because you can’t go there at night. The drawbridge closes, preventing you from accessing the town after sunset. Luckily, you have the Sun Song to quickly change night into day, allowing you to enter the town.

This isn’t an issue, however, in the remake, as the town is constantly open to you. You can come and go as you please at any time of the day or night without anyone getting upset with you. You may have had it in your mind to keep going during the day, or maybe you just assumed that the gate was open and forgot that it closed in the original.

Fairy Thoughts didn’t exist in the original game. Instead, they are something new that is specific to the Ocarina of Time Remake. These small glowing symbols can be found on various surfaces around Hyrule, even in dungeons. Sometimes Fairy Thoughts act as hints to help you progress through the game, and other times they are small puzzles that fully restore Link’s health once they are solved.

They are a neat little change that you might not have noticed while exploring, as they can be easy to overlook. I didn’t notice them for a long time, and since I found one, I have been going around looking for more.

Link has always been known as the silent hero of Hyrule, but the remake appears to have given him a very brief spoken line.

You may have seen various little whirlwinds around Hyrule in the remake. These are used to summon the scarecrow, and they didn’t appear in the original. In the original Ocarina of Time, if you wanted to summon Pierre, you needed to find a spot where Navi would glow green instead of the normal blue. This indicated that it was a spot where the scarecrow song could be played.

Now, if you want to summon Pierre the Wandering Scarecrow, you simply need to find a place where “the straw swirls in the wind.” Which is any location with a bit of swirling wind. At least these locations are easier to find.

There are some who received the Giant’s Knife from Goron City back in the day, swung it around to test it, and then ultimately got disappointed when it broke before they even left the area and got to test it on some enemies. For those who don’t know, this weapon is very fragile, making it so it breaks after just eight hits. It is a cautionary tale that teaches everyone that nothing is permanent, except the Master Sword.

Anyway, the weapon still breaks in the remake, but there has been a change. Nintendo removed the hitboxes from walls, so you can swing the weapon around and not have it break off the environment. Instead, it will break from striking enemies, as was intended.

The Biggoron Sword is quite powerful, and in the original game, many replaced the Master Sword with it because it could be swung at the same pace and it hit harder. The only difference was you couldn’t use your shield while wielding it. Despite that drawback, the Biggoron Sword was worth holding onto, as an experienced swordfighter didn’t need to worry about using their shield for the most part.

This sword has been changed in the remake. It is still massive, and requires both hands to swing. However, the swing speed of it is noticeably slower, making it more difficult to hit some enemies with the blade. This put more emphasis on the use of the Master Sword in certain situations.

Since The Ocarina of Time is a third-person title, you might not have realized that there was a first-person option in the original. The game did go into first-person when shooting your slingtshot, but otherwise, you needed to press a button for it, and even then it was temporary.

The remake of the beloved title doesn’t even give you the option to go into first-person mode. Instead, it keeps you tied to the third-person camera. This is a bit of a strange change from the original and one that some people discovered right away, as they used to use first-person mode to get a closer look at the environment. To replace it, many have said that Nintendo should have added a photo mode.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has finally been released, and fans have already discovered several game-breaking glitches.

One of the side quests you can complete in Ocarina of Time is the one for the Happy Mask Salesman. This quest requires you to purchase various masks and sell them to citizens of Hyrule. However, in the original, you weren’t allowed to wear the masks as an adult. People always thought this was a bit strange, but it is a detail that didn’t matter much.

The remake, on the other hand, allows you to wear the various masks as an adult. There isn’t anything special about wearing the masks as an adult versus wearing them as a kid, but it is an interesting little detail that Nintendo added that wasn’t in the original game.

After progressing through the game, you finally make your way to the Spirit Temple. This is one of my personal favorite temples in the game, and like the other temples in the game, it has undergone some changes in the remake.

One of the more peculiar changes is the one made to the large Gerudo statue in the temple. In the original, certain parts of the statue were able to be grappled using your hookshot, but there were never any obvious grapple points. This has been changed in the remake, with the statue still being there, but the grapple points are now gone, so you can no longer grab the statue if it’s something that interests you.

This is a bit of an odd change, but one that people are thankful has been made. In the original Ocarina of Time, when you reach the Zora’s Domain, you talk to King Zora, and you eventually get him to scoot out of the way so you can visit Lord Jabu-Jabu. This scoot is obnoxiously long, as King Zora likes to take his time getting out of your way.

Well, in the remake, King Zora still scoots out of the way, but the change is that Nintendo made is significantly quicker. When timed, King Zora moves out of the way roughly eight seconds faster than he does in the original Ocarina of Time. Thankfully, we only need to wait around 20 seconds now instead of almost 30. Nintendo kept this hilarious if frustrating part of the title in, but streamlined it considerably.

Some of the original's most charming quirks from Zelda: Ocarina of Time didn't make the journey.

#4184. MSI 2027 heads to Valencia as Riot reshapes Split 1 with First Stand: All In in China

Riot will take the Mid-Season Invitational to Spain in 2027, bringing a top-tier League of Legends event back to Europe for the first time since the Worlds 2024 final in London. Its one-off, expanded First Stand in China will also change Split 1 for the LEC, with the full details due in January.

Europe will host a top-tier League of Legends event again in 2027. Riot set out its international calendar on 13 November, the eve of the Worlds 2026 final. The Mid-Season Invitational goes to Valencia. London’s staging of the Worlds 2024 final was the last time the continent held an international League of Legends tournament.

For British fans, that puts a top-tier event within Europe next year. Riot has not yet given dates or ticket details for the Feria de Valencia event.

Spain’s last international League of Legends event came in 2019. That year, Madrid’s Palacio Vistalegre staged the Worlds quarter-finals and semi-finals. Valencia has never hosted one before.

China will stage First Stand: All In at the start of the 2027 season. Riot calls this single edition its largest tournament ever.

First Stand 2027 had originally been given to Southeast Asia. The bigger format took it to China instead. Southeast Asia will now host the event in 2028.

The change reaches every regional league, including the LEC. The larger event will change Split 1, just as Fnatic, G2 and the other LEC teams rebuild their rosters. In 2026, First Stand ran from 16 to 22 March, between the two regional splits. A bigger event at the start of the year leaves less certainty about how that window will look in 2027.

Riot has not yet said how many teams will take part or how they will qualify. Until then, LEC teams are building squads without knowing how many European places are on offer.

Worlds 2027 will be shared between two countries. The Swiss Stage goes to Nagoya, Japan. The quarter-finals and semi-finals move to the Suwon Convention Center in South Korea. The title decider goes to Seoul Arena, which is still under construction.

The arena was 81% built on 23 October. Work is due to finish in May 2027, with the venue opening in June 2027.

The city is backing the event with public money. Seoul has set aside 1.369 billion won (about US$1.02 million) in its proposed 2027 budget to host the Worlds final and Fan Fest, Sheep Esports reported.

The 2026 calendar offers a reference point for the circuit’s rhythm. MSI ran from 28 June to 12 July, and Worlds from 15 October to 14 November. Riot has not confirmed whether the 2027 events will follow similar windows.

For LEC teams, clarity on the season opener in China is due in January.

#4183. Thrifty Business review - "The coziest management sim you'll ever play"

I never thought I'd come across something that manages to impress me to this extent - until Thrifty Business, at least. And let me tell you: I was beyond impressed. So, this is not just a simple Thrifty Business review; this is me telling you why you need to give it a try.

I play a lot of games. And by a lot, I mean A LOT. So, at this point, it takes quite a bit for something to genuinely surprise me.

I expected a cute little shop management sim (as per the Play Store images). Maybe something to play for a few hours and decorate a few shelves. Well, it didn't happen quite like that. I ended up spending far more time than I'd expected rearranging furniture and getting excited over witchy items.

In essence, you can buy unwanted items from NPCs in the form of mystery boxes. Then, you place them on the shelves and organise them by category. Later on, you can even organise events and expand. That's it.

Honestly, what's not to love? Grab your tea and blanket and get cosy - we'll talk gameplay! In terms of gameplay, you have all the freedom you need as a shopkeeper. You can genuinely make the place feel like your own. From finding the perfect spot for an item to rearranging displays, you're the boss.

You can even redecorate as much as you like - there's no restriction on that (thankfully), so in a way, you can play this in your own way. I mean, you can even skip decorating altogether and just play for the dialogue or for making money.

Personally, I'm always going to choose decorating over anything else, even at the cost of buying additional items.

On the topic of additional items, Thrifty Business doesn't try to turn running a shop into a stressful experience. There's no pressure to maximise every penny or deal with impatient customers.

Even if you end up making no sales in a day, the system still has a way to keep you progressing by offering a free mystery box every day. Not that they're particularly expensive (at the beginning, at least), but it's little details like this that make me appreciate the thought put into the experience.

Just a fair warning though: it's the kind of sim where you tell yourself "I'll play for another ten minutes", only to realise an entire hour flew by. The pixel graphics: love at first sight Can we please talk about the aesthetics?

The colourful 90s atmosphere makes the entire experience feel like a warm hug.

As someone who grew up during that time, seeing all those nostalgic items brought into 2026 put a smile on my face. I'd almost forgotten all about the Slinky!

Since I mentioned it, let me make one thing clear: there are a lot of items you can acquire in Thrifty Business. I mean A LOT. With so many of them, it's hard not to appreciate the sheer amount of work that must have gone into designing all those individual sprites. Not everyone's cup of tea - but maybe everyone's cup of hot cocoa? I have to admit, Thrifty Business understands exactly what kind of experience it wants to offer. It's not one of those fast-paced tycoons where you rush to make millions from the get-go.

That might not make it into everyone's favourite list, but it is bound to make it into some. If you're over here reading this and you have someone special in your life who likes Stardew Valley, then Thrifty Business is something you can definitely surprise them with.

Really, sometimes, all you need is to escape into a cute little world, put things on shelves, decorate to your heart's content, and call it a day. Life is too fast-paced sometimes anyway, and Thrifty Business can be the escape that is one tap away. You need to play with the sound on The audio deserves some love too, and I believe Spellgarden Games did an amazing job creating a soundtrack that perfectly complements the sim. I honestly couldn't fault it at all, and I'm usually the type to turn the sound off after spending more than five hours with a game. Not this time, though...

An ode to the queer community As if the cosy atmosphere wasn't enough, I absolutely adore the queer representation woven into this.

From the story (which you should absolutely read - I won't give you any spoilers) to the item categories and even character creation, there's something about the sense of community you get in this little virtual world that gives you a fuzzy feeling inside. Not too many games celebrate individuality, self-expression, and simply being yourself in a way that feels "just right".

Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a shop to rearrange. Again.

#4181. Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

The first Battlefield 6 patch of the year is almost here, bringing a smattering of changes, including one that doesn't quite make sense.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

The patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

Arguably, one of the main elements that gives the Grand Theft Auto series its powerful, widespread appeal is its congruity with modern film and television. It’s an extremely cinematic series, both in and out of actual gameplay, with a particular emphasis on building strong narratives and compelling characters. Given all of that, the idea of pursuing a live-action adaptation of the series, either in the form of a television series or a feature film, seems kind of obvious.

With the looming release of Grand Theft Auto 6 and the immeasurable hype it’s brought with it, not to mention the recent success of video game adaptations in both film and TV like the live-action Fallout series or the new season of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, it might just be a perfect time to start shopping the GTA IP around for other media avenues.

In an interview with The David Rubenstein Show podcast, relayed via Deadline, Take-Two Interactive’s CEO, Strauss Zelnick, admitted that the idea has naturally crossed his and his company’s collective minds, and the chance is definitely not zero. However, if it were to happen, it could only happen in a very particular circumstance.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

In the interview, Zelnick was asked how he felt about “line extensions” in regard to the GTA IP. In other words, branches out into other forms of media and licensing beyond just video games, which would naturally include television and film.

“We’re very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth – entertainment we’re always proud of,” Zelnick responded.

Zelnick explained that Take-Two and Rockstar could absolutely head up a live-action adaptation of GTA, either a specific game or the franchise as a whole, but he’d only be willing to give it the green light if absolutely everyone involved were completely and totally committed and confident.

We’re very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth.

If the creative teams weren’t just confident that a hypothetical movie or show would be well-liked by viewers, but willing to tackle the task with genuine, uncompromising passion, it simply wouldn’t meet his standards.

“It’s a high bar to do that, and of course, there’s always a risk of failure. So we don’t rule it out, but we’re very, very selective,” Zelnick cautioned.

I don’t think it’d be hyperbolic to say that Take-Two Interactive and Rockstar Games are about to make a lot of money, to put it very mildly. The world is spinning on the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, and with pre-order profits through the roof and critics already singing praises, this game is slated to become one of the definitive faces of the gaming industry and a tentpole of current pop culture besides.

All of that is to say that, given recent trends in the broader entertainment sphere, I have a feeling a lot of doors are about to open to GTA as an IP. Not that they were previously closed per se, as the series’ previous games were all exceptionally popular and profitable. Rather, the sphere seems a lot more willing to jump on gaming bandwagons than it was even a decade ago, and if GTA 6 pulls the kinds of numbers it’s projected to, the proverbial phone is going to be ringing off the hook with offers and deals.

We’re probably not going to see a GTA show or movie in the immediate future, but with the cash and resources Take-Two will undoubtedly accrue from this release, it could manifest sooner than we expect.

Sam Houser offered up a rare statement ahead of what might just be the biggest video game launch in modern history.

#4177. Battlefield 6’s first big map in months is coming to Labs soon, but I'm more excited about BF4's Golmud Railway making its way to BF6

As promised, Battlefield Labs is coming back to bring us a preview of some of Battlefield 6’s upcoming Season 2 content.

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a big component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the new maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios says the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

The blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of big maps as Battlefield 6 currently is.

Another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

More Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off new gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

Battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios said we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

Ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

There’s even more exciting news for fans of big maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is currently in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

For context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its issues elsewhere, and BF Studios says it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

Finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

Redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.

#4176. Path to Nowhere tier list - All characters ranked

Updated on November 2nd, 2026 - Version: 1.9.54

Path to Nowhere has a considerable variety of characters you can unlock. But if you are a beginner, finding out what hero to use can be problematic. Luckily, experts across the web have created a tier list for Path to Nowhere to solve this problem.

We have similar articles like this Neural Cloud tier list and Summoners War: Chronicles tier list, where we have also ranked all of the characters by their power and abilities from the best to worst. If you're playing different mobile games, try to search around - our website is brimming with tier lists and various guides for the most popular games. WHAT IS THE PATH TO NOWHERE TIER LIST?

This Path to Nowhere tier list is similar to the ones we have for other video games. There are four tiers: S, A, B, and C. Continue reading, and you will learn more about every tier.

Most players consider Demon to be the most overpowered hero in the game. His special attack stacks a shield for him and his allies. The more health points Demon has, the more powerful protection he will create.

He also has potent attack stats, allowing him to kill enemies fast.

Nox is the most accessible hero in Tier S. She can be unlocked by completing the 14-day event. Nox has incredibly high DPS and a passive ability that decreases your enemies’ defence. Moreover, Nox increases attack points upon killing enemies, which is one of the best abilities in Path to Nowhere. So, make sure to obtain this hero as soon as you can.

Labyrinth is the only hero in Tier S that has a B rarity. So, you can unlock her even if you don't play the game daily. Labyrinth is a damage dealer who takes the primary role in a team. She can break enemies’ shields and even destroy Demon’s shield.

Even though Baiyi has less DPS than Nox, she still can deal a lot of damage in a short period. Moreover, her skill significantly increases critical rate boost. She is also one of the fastest heroes in Path to Nowhere.

Langley is a top-level hero because of her particular skill. It provides you with an AoE attack that can hit a 3x3 area. So, Langley is a perfect option if you want to fight against bosses or groups of enemies.

Eirene is a magical attacker that probably has one of the best passive abilities in the game. While using an auto-attack, she creates a black hole that hits a 3x3 area. The only disadvantage is that Eirene is weak in melee fights.

Hamel is the only healer in Path to Nowhere that is worth being in Tier S. She has an AoE healing effect that helps keep your team's HP topped up in battle.

Countless Chelsea is one of the most complex heroes in Path to Nowhere. But in good hands, she brings excellent results. Countless Chelsea can summon a panther that can be used as a shield. Also, she has damage reduction, allowing her to take a lot of punishment and still survive.

The main feature of Demolia is her health points. She can quickly increase them and, after that, heal herself, which significantly increases her survivability. The only reason why she's not in Tier S is that there is a limit on her HP boost and healing.

Even though Serpent looks cute, she is one of the deadliest heroes in Path to Nowhere. While using a standard attack, she applies a slowdown effect to enemies and increases her speed. Moreover, when there are no enemies near Serpent, she will raise her attack.

RouLecca has poor DPS and can only deal damage using critical attacks, but she can increase her crit rate and damage while attacking.

Zoya is the Tier A hero most likely to appear in Tier S in the future. She has a 3x3 AoE attack that can deal significant damage. Zoya also has a lot of health points and has no problem killing enemies in short range. But the best thing about Zoya is her passive skill. It increases her attacking speed, making her suitable even in the later stages of the game.

Pricilla can summon a clone who helps her during battle. Additionally, she has high DPS, allowing you to kill enemies quickly. Unfortunately, her lack of health points doesn't make her worthy of becoming Tier S.

Hecate's ability has long range and hits every target in this range, which is extremely powerful. But Hecate doesn't have good survivability, so you should be careful while using her.

Aerial is the only healer in Tier A. The only difference between her and Hamel is that she is universal. Aerial has increased damage, which enables her to fight against enemies. And for increased damage, she gives up her healing capabilities. So, Aerial can't heal as effectively as Hamel.

Victoria is a hero with really significant damage. However, she forgoes health points for such a high attack capability. She will lower her health points to gain more attacks and kill enemies more effectively.

Luvia Ray is the most classic damage dealer in Path to Nowhere. She has high stats and a passive skill oriented toward increasing attack. Overall, she is a mighty hero who will always bring benefit to your team.

Crache has one of the best special attacks in the game. The AoE can deal a high amount of damage quickly. Moreover, this attack has an unblocking effect, so that opponents can't dodge it. The only disadvantage of Crache is that she has purely physical stats. Therefore, she must be complemented by powerful characters who can deal a lot of damage.

The best thing about EMP is that this hero is free. You can obtain her by completing the first chapter of the story. As for battle, she is perfectly suitable for the role of a background hero. Her special attack can wipe out low HP heroes and provide additional buffs for your team.

Tier B includes the following characters:

You can find out more about the most powerful heroes from Tier B below.

Cinnabar is a unique combination of powerful abilities in one character. She can create a 3x3 range shield protecting allies. Even though this shield doesn't have many health points, using it can still be handy during battles. Overall, Cinnabar is pretty powerful. She has a strong multiplier, allowing her to win battles easily.

Ninety-Nine is one of the best tanks in Path to Nowhere. You can exchange her health points in order to deal damage to enemies. On top of that, her extraordinary ability will reduce her health to get a significant attack bonus.

Sumire hits four times in a row in the same direction with her Special Ability. This special is extremely powerful on small maps, making Sumire more effective there. Also, she increases her damage when someone is opposite to her. Moreover, there are no limitations on increasing damage.

Even though Wolverine can't play the central role in the team, his slowing-down effect allows him to be effective even with higher-tier characters. Wolverine has special traps that stun enemies. These traps have a high range, making this hero super helpful.

Tier C includes characters that aren't recommended to use, even if you are a beginner.

The main feature of Pepper is her powerful attack speed. She can even increase it using a particular skill. But the main problem with Pepper is that she has no other stats to boast about.

There is nothing special about Gekkabijin. She has no powerful stats like the Tier S characters. Her unique ability provides her with additional attack and shield, but it isn't good enough to be competitive nowadays.

Even though the game has different characters with distinct abilities, it's best to only use the ones at the top of our Path to Nowhere tier list if you can - Tier S and Tier A - since they consistently perform the best.

Thank you for reading this guide - hope you find it helpful! And while you are here, make sure to read our Path to Nowhere beginner's guide as well.

#4175. Arc Raiders finally reveals early 2026 roadmap, but we’re not getting a new map for a while

The first couple of months of 2026 in the world of Arc Raiders look pretty promising, but the big guns are being held back for now.

After weeks of waiting, Arc Raiders developer Embark has officially unveiled the first few months of the game’s 2026 roadmap. The plan is split into four months, covering January to April, collectively dubbed Escalation.

We’re expecting a content update each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one new map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

While we wait for that, Arc Raiders is going to go through several events and other in-game changes, some more meaningful (and exciting) than others. January looks to be the lightest so far, which makes sense given that it’s just a week or so from ending.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a new matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

Things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a new Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

Interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map update during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a new Expedition Window.

The Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another new Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an update to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

Finally, April is when the big guns come out, because that’s when the first new map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.

#4173. GTA 6 Just Broke Twitch's Biggest Viewership Record In Just 30 Minutes

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

If you thought the hype surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6 couldn't possibly get any bigger, the game's launch has already found a way to prove you wrong! After becoming one of the highest-rated games ever, more impressive numbers are popping up.

While most players are still waiting for November 19 to arrive (less than 24 hours now, folks!), fans in regions like New Zealand have already gotten their hands on Rockstar's long-awaited open-world adventure. And it took just minutes for the game to make streaming history.

According to data from Streams Charts, GTA 6 already attracted more than 5.3 million concurrent viewers across major livestreaming platforms shortly after becoming available in New Zealand. That figure was already enough to smash the previous record for a video game launch, and the numbers have continued climbing as the release rolls out to more countries.

By the time the game became available in Japan and South Korea, its combined audience had reached an astonishing 7.18 million concurrent viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick. And that's before every other region has even had a chance to jump into Vice City!

Sam Houser offered up a rare statement ahead of what might just be the biggest video game launch in modern history.

To put things in a broader perspective, the previous record for the biggest video game launch in streaming history belonged to Valorant. Riot Games' shooter attracted approximately 1.74 million concurrent viewers during its closed beta in April 2020, a number that seemed almost impossible to beat at the time.

Well, GTA 6 has more than quadrupled that figure. According to Streams Charts' preliminary data, the game currently leads its ranking of the biggest game launches by Peak Viewers with 7,183,979 concurrent viewers. Hogwarts Legacy follows in third place with approximately 1.36 million, while Path of Exile 2 and Lost Ark round out the top five.

By the time the game became available in Japan and South Korea, its combined audience had reached an astonishing 7.18 million concurrent viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick.

The numbers are particularly impressive considering that the game's worldwide release is still underway. As more players gain access, additional streamers are expected to go live, potentially pushing the record even higher!

It is also worth looking at how the audience is distributed across platforms. Twitch currently leads with a peak of 3.06 million viewers, followed by YouTube with 2.74 million and Kick with 1.36 million. Twitch's figure makes GTA 6 the second-most-watched gaming category in the platform's history, narrowly behind League of Legends and its 3.11 million peak.

12.5 million American gamers plan to adjust their schedules for Rockstar's next big release.

Besides, the game's launch has also been an important moment for individual creators. Streams Charts reports that HoneyMad currently leads the list of streamers with the highest concurrent audiences, reaching 576,313 viewers on Twitch. And Brazilian streamer alanzoka also had a huge launch, setting a new personal record with 313,548 live viewers.

And to be completely honest, it is hard to imagine anyone being particularly surprised by these numbers! GTA 5 has remained one of the biggest games on streaming platforms for more than a decade, and its successor has arrived with an unprecedented level of anticipation.

Of course, it is important to remember that these figures are still preliminary. Streams Charts notes that its latest data was collected at 12:30 UTC on November 18, and the numbers are expected to change as the game becomes available in more regions. Still, GTA 6 has already accomplished something no other game launch has managed before. If this is what the first few hours look like, I can't wait to see what happens once everyone can finally play.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

#4172. Void/Breaker Review – Chaos Is The Point

Many games tout impressive destruction systems under the hood, but few implement it as well as Void/Breaker. The ruin is visually spectacular, sure – who doesn’t love to watch buildings crumble because of your grenade or gravity-thrown explosives? But importantly, it’s a critical aspect of Void/Breaker’s roguelite design. Enemies caught beneath falling rubble become instantly staggered, and that’s your moment to kill. Grenades do this too, as do most items you throw at the hostile AI machinery trying to end your run, creating a vortex of shifting priorities as you dash, jump, and shoot at sequential staggered enemies in your sightlines. Countless weapon mods and permutations make fewer than a dozen weapons feel like hundreds in your arsenal, adding even more blissful chaos to the mix. Though it can be difficult at times, if you can see through the literal remains of your destruction, one of the year’s most engaging shooters awaits.

Void/Breaker wastes no time getting a gun in your hand. An AI voice in your head wants your help escaping a simulation where thousands of runners attempt to reach the end of multi-arena stages to defeat a boss. He asks that you simply follow the simulation’s commands; meanwhile, he uses the data you collect along the way to find new exits for you and him. The storytelling style is very reminiscent of Valve’s Portal. Something much larger is at play here, but it’s worth discovering for yourself.

This narrative framework supports the game’s roguelite structure. Mechanically, however, you enter various themed digital stages, from liminal spaces to beaches to snow-capped cliffs and more, and attempt to survive. Most arenas consist of a couple of starkly white structures that your grenades and thrown explosives can topple (ideally onto waves of enemies below). Learning the language of Void/Breaker means constantly scanning your field of view for explosives and structures practically begging to come down, and then eyeing neon-green bars above enemies that tell you they’re staggered and ready for a quick kill. Developer Stubby Games throws plenty of wrenches into this formula, like armored foes and electrostatic enemies you must melee first, and elite bots that will have you on the back foot, but for the most part, Void/Breaker’s formula is “Break stuff, then kill.”

The game emphasizes explosives and bringing buildings down, but your guns do most of the killing; you can only select one weapon per run. You choose from a pistol, shotgun, machine gun, sniper, and more, and each has its perks (though once I unlocked the SMG, I rarely picked anything else). There’s no sense overthinking your weapon, though, because the dozens of mods you pick up each run determine its effectiveness. As you pick up more schematics, the pool of mods you find in chests or drop from enemies expands, and soon your gun fires corrosive acid, electricity, fire, projectile missiles, and more. Not to mention, mods change how the gun fires, how much damage certain bullets do, recoil, accuracy, and just about any other stat you associate with firing a video game gun. Wild combinations are easy to create, and a unique mod-stacking mechanic that can double or triple effectiveness adds a light touch of puzzle design to this otherwise straight shooter.

Stubby Games smartly emphasizes player expression, never getting in the way of the zanier combinations available to players. The SMG I used to beat the final boss featured mods that made each bullet electric, shot missiles with each shot, covered each bullet in a destructive orb, and featured a ricochet perk that made each bullet bounce off walls and split into even more bullets. I’m thankful for mid-run saves because this SMG permutation, paired with an ability mod that let me throw infinite grenades for a limited time, filled my screen with so much destruction that the entire game crashed. I’d usually bemoan such a thing, but I couldn’t help but laugh. I pushed my PC to its limit with my on-screen chaos.

Boss fights leave a little to be desired – I rarely died because of their simple bullet-hell arenas. Instead, most runs ended because, after bringing down every structure around me, I’d get so lost in the chaos that I wouldn't realize I was stuck in debris while enemies swarmed my location. As stunning as it is to see so much happening on screen, it can be hard to understand what is going on during the most chaotic moments.

Between enemy-filled arenas en route to a stage’s end boss, you might find a shop to buy more mods, ominous obelisks with risk-reward propositions (gain a lot of health or lose half your health, for example), optional trials, and strange phenomena that transport you to different locations. These moments are quick breaks in between bouts of adrenaline-fueled shooter action that I always welcomed – enemies can be relentless, especially as new types are introduced in each stage.

The rest of the Void/Breaker package offers few genre surprises. You can upgrade various traits between runs, research new mod schematics to add to the random pool, purchase new weapons, and discover fun secrets. You can unlock shortcuts, glean in-world information from computer terminals, and hear intriguing dialogue barks from the AI partner who needs your help. It’s all standard stuff for the rogue genre, but if anything, its simplicity pushes you back to the meat and potatoes of this shooter.

Void/Breaker’s shorter runtime – I rolled credits at 12 hours – ensures nothing gets too repetitive in its roguelite structure, but an expansive endgame promises even more to engage with, like different run modifications you can enable to make an already chaotic shooter even more anarchic. I’ll certainly be running it back (again and again) to see what other disruptions I can bring to this AI-simulated adventure. It’s hard not to when destruction feels this good.

#4171. Bilibili Gaming beat all four LCK teams to win Worlds 2026 and end Korean title run

Bilibili Gaming beat Gen.G in Brooklyn to win the 2026 League of Legends World Championship, the LPL's first world title since 2021. Added to their First Stand trophy, the result gives a Chinese side a double that no team had managed since 2016, just as Riot takes the 2027 season opener to China.

Bilibili Gaming are world champions. The LPL side needed four games to beat Gen.G in New York and win the club’s first Worlds title. The result ends a run of four straight LCK world titles. It also gives the LPL its first world crown since EDward Gaming won in 2021.

BLG took the hardest possible route. They knocked out all four LCK teams at the event: Hanwha Life Esports, Dplus KIA, T1 and Gen.G. Every Korean side that travelled to the tournament went home after facing them.

The final turned early. BLG levelled the series at 1-1 by winning a 53-minute second game. It was the longest game of the whole tournament. Gen.G had reached the final with two 3-0 knockout wins, over LYON on 4 November and Invictus Gaming on 7 November.

For Knight, the MVP award closes a loop. The BLG mid laner lost the 2024 final to T1. Two years later, he finished on the winning side.

The runners-up looked inward after the defeat. At Gen.G’s post-final press conference, Chovy said the team had broken its own rules. Duro, playing his first Worlds, regretted that they had dropped their drafting plan.

Gen.G still leave with US$800,000 as runners-up. Semi-finalists T1 and Invictus Gaming received US$400,000 each. Riot ran the event from 15 October to 14 November with 19 teams.

Gen.G’s admission points to the draft as a weak spot. The figures support a narrower reading too. Gen.G swept both knockout opponents before the final. Against BLG, they could not hold the lead after taking the opening game.

Worlds was BLG’s second international trophy of the year. In March they won the First Stand Tournament in São Paulo. They beat G2 Esports 3-1 in that final and collected the US$250,000 top prize.

Winning both events makes BLG the first team since SK Telecom T1 in 2016 to take more than one major international title in a year.

#4170. Nioh 3’s generous demo is out now, and your progress carries over to the full game

If you’re looking for a way to check out one of the biggest releases of early 2026, Team Ninja has made it easy for you.

Nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously announced demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

Unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty new for the series, which has typically launched first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

The Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

Another big reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

The demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

This time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

Pokémon Masters EX, the officially licensed game by DeNA, has brought tons of new Sync Pairs for players to collect and use with their fifth anniversary. #4168. EDward Gaming part with CHICHOO and nobody as Champions core breaks up before 2027

EDward Gaming have lost captain nobody and CHICHOO, two days after releasing Smoggy to Bilibili Gaming. The VCT China partner team must now rebuild before the China Kickoff in Hangzhou in January.

EDward Gaming have parted ways with CHICHOO and captain nobody, two pillars of the side that won VALORANT Champions 2024. Both players left the VCT China partner team on the same day. EDG announced both exits on Weibo. Their exits end a five-year spell at the organisation.

The departures follow quickly on from Smoggy’s move to Bilibili Gaming. Within a week, three players had gone from the EDG roster. No replacements have been named.

Wang ‘nobody’ Senxu joined EDG on 7 September 2021. He served as the team’s captain and in-game leader. He had started out as the side’s Initiator before taking on those leadership duties. CHICHOO, whose full name is Wan Shunzhi, played the Controller role. Alongside CHICHOO, he formed the core of the only Chinese team to win Champions. That title, sealed on 25 August 2024, made EDG the first organisation from China, and from Asia, to lift the trophy. The team’s total winnings stand at roughly $1,592,287.

The pair were still central to the side in 2026. At Masters London, CHICHOO and nobody each played 12 maps. Their average combat scores were 179 and 184 respectively. EDG finished third in London and earned $125,000. Their run ended with a 0-3 defeat to Leviatán in the lower bracket final on 20 June 2026.

Where nobody goes next is not yet confirmed. Sheep Esports reported, citing sources, that he is expected to join Trace Esports for 2027. Trace’s Kai and deLb are said to be under contract until the end of 2027. If that move happens, nobody and Smoggy would both start the new season with different organisations.

The timing is awkward for EDG. The organisation was named a VCT partner team on 21 October, on a two-year contract. That deal now begins with a heavily changed roster.

The China Kickoff is an S-Tier LAN event. It is organised by TJ Sports, Hero Esports and Riot Games. The league’s partner sides make up eight places in the field, with the remaining four split evenly between visiting teams and open qualifier entrants. EDG will need a settled line-up in place to compete there.

He is expected to go to Trace Esports 🇨🇳 with CHICHOO 🇨🇳 pic.twitter.com/ReRLcovmLe

Wuhan hosts Cup 1 from 29 April to 23 May, and Shanghai stages Cup 2 from 5 to 29 August. Before either, the Kickoff in January is the first test for EDG’s rebuilt side.

#4167. Quantic Dream addresses toxicity, tech bugs and tutorials for Spellcasters Chronicles closed beta 2 - here's how to get a key

Here are the start and end times for the second Spellcasters Chronicles closed beta, as well as what's new in this latest test.

Quantic Dream has opened up its upcoming fantasy MOBA for a second closed beta weekend starting from today, January 29, until 9AM UTC on Monday February 2.

The closed beta is for PC only in Europe, Asia and North America and potential players can register to join the waitlist for a key at the game’s official website or on the Spellcasters Chronicles Steam page. Players who had access to the first closed beta will automatically have access to the second, but you can sign up on both the site and Steam to increase your chances of entry.

The MOBA genre is competitive in every sense and Quantic Dream is trying to break into it with a Magic the Gathering-esque spin on the format. Players build a deck of cards before queuing into teams of 3, then face off as battling mages, summoning creatures, building fortifications and casting spells rather than choosing a Hero with unique abilities in the traditional MOBA style.

Beta content includes a new map, 6 new spells and 5 new summon creatures for your deck, as well as 3 new buildings too.

Also new for this second closed beta is an introduction and tutorial for some of the game’s finer details, as well as a text chat for strategising and much-needed player reporting system to go with it. It will also feature early versions of the Spellcaster customisation system and ranked matches.

Spellcasters Chronicles is the first ever multiplayer online game from Quantic Dream, the French studio best known for cinematic narrative games like Detroit: Become Human, Heavy Rain and Beyond: Two Souls.

A TV adaptation of the latter game is reportedly in development, or the rights for one have been acquired at least. Elsewhere, Quantic Dream’s long-rumoured game in the Star Wars franchise was revealed as Star Wars Eclipse, a return-to-type narrative action game set in the High Republic era of a galaxy far, far away.

#4166. 8 Mistakes Everyone Made When Playing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Many of us grew up with the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and were excited when The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake was announced. We had years upon years to play the original title, and it has honed our skills for the remake.

Of course, that is what everyone thought, and then when each of us started the remake we all started making numerous mistakes. Maybe you completely forgot about the sprint button, or maybe you completely forgot that you can manually jump now.

There are a bunch of mistakes that are easy to make when you have the muscle memory of the original game baked into your being.

The original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is known for not having a dedicated jump button. Actually many of the early Zelda titles didn’t have a dedicated jump button. Of course, this was changed in the remake, and Nintendo made sure that everyone was aware of that.

When the remake was finally shown off, Nintendo made sure to emphasize that you could manually jump instead of relying on hitting a ledge. Despite this, I know I am not the only one who walked off a ledge.

Even though Nintendo told everyone about the jump button, we all ran to a ledge and muscle memory took over, so instead of jumping, we all just fell off into the water around Kokiri Forest.

Autosave has been around in games for a long time, but it didn’t always exist. Back in the day, you needed to manually save all of your games or you lost your data when things went south.

I know multiple people who gave up playing Ocarina of Time for a bit because they forgot to save. Now, you don’t need to worry about it, as there is an autosave feature in the remake.

I can’t be the only one who relied entirely on the autosave. In fact, I didn’t manually save for the first few hours of playing the game, and it came back to bite me later on. Make sure you always save your game and don’t just assume the autosave has your back.

Zelda Notes statistics reveal that the most common causes of death are surprisingly embarrassing.

There are some classic Rupee exploits we used to perform in the original Ocarina of Time, with one of the most obvious being the drawbridge jump. When you climbed the chains attached to the drawbridge, you could make some easy money by jumping off along the wall.

This would get you red Rupees, which are worth 20 Rupees, and that went a long way towards purchasing some important items. However, these exploits don’t work anymore.

The remake has removed the exploits from days past, and now we must rely on new exploits to gather a bunch of Rupees in a quick manner, but that doesn’t mean we all didn’t try it anyway.

After we beat the original Ocarina of Time, it became a habit to want to beat it as fast as possible, and thus, the insane number of speedrun attempts started, making Ocarina of Time one of the most replayed games in history.

If you were someone who tried to speedrun the game over and over again, you might have tried to perform one of the speedrunning tactics only to find that they just don’t work anymore. Nintendo didn’t even purposefully leave any in as a tribute.

However, that hasn’t stopped gamers from figuring out many of the remake’s glitches. Now you can skip straight to the Shadow Temple after leaving Kokiri Forest.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has finally been released, and fans have already discovered several game-breaking glitches.

After you play through a game enough, you remember the various details, like where a key is supposed to be, or the layout of a dungeon. There are many people who remember the layouts of every dungeon in Ocarina of Time like the back of their hand.

All this muscle memory doesn’t help in the remake, as the dungeons have been redesigned. Some of the rooms are different, and there are even some new areas to explore that weren’t in the original.

It has made the remake feel like a brand new Zelda title rather than the same old game everyone is used to, but the fact remains that you probably thought a room would be in a specific place and ended up running into a wall.

Redeads were terrifying when in the original Ocarina of Time. Their lifeless bodies freaked out many kids back in the day, and Nintendo managed to keep that same feeling alive in the remake.

Many people, like myself, underestimated the newer version of the Redeads. Nintendo made them much quicker this time around, and it is very easy to get caught in their screams.

I went into the game thinking I would easily take them down, and I do now, but at first, I was grabbed, and it took me off guard. They are much more menacing this time around and shouldn’t be taken lightly.

Motion controls can be the bane of anyone’s existence if they aren’t prepared for them. Back in the day, Nintendo didn’t have motion controls in games, meaning those who grew up with the original Ocarina of Time didn’t need to worry about them.

However, since the Nintendo Switch 2 has motion controls, Nintendo decided to turn them on for the start of the Ocarina of Time Remake. If you didn’t know this, it became very apparent when playing the slingshot mini-game.

As soon as I started the mini-game, something felt off, and I quickly noticed that my aim was being controlled by my movement. I am not the only one who didn’t realize motion controls were automatically turned on, and we all quickly turned them off.

Remember, if you want to use your slingshot, you need to be a kid. If you want to use your bow, you need to be an adult. This is a very common mistake that was made in the original, and now it is common to make in the remake.

Child Link and adult Link have two different inventories. Some items that work for you as a kid, don’t work when you are an adult and vice-versa. This can be a bit annoying, especially since an adult definitely knows how to use a boomerang.

Anyway, it is a mistake that we have all made, as it is easy to play as one version of Link for a while, switch to the other version, and then forget what items you have access to.

Some of the original's most charming quirks from Zelda: Ocarina of Time didn't make the journey.
