#4165. Tower of Fantasy tier list - Best weapons and characters for PVE and PVP

Updated on November 18th, 2026 - Version: 6.3.0 - Recently Added: Zoey

Do you want to know what the best weapons and characters are in Tower of Fantasy? Then hop into our Tower of Fantasy tier list, which will guide you through all the weapons and characters currently available, as well as their features and what they bring to the team!

Tower of Fantasy is a long-awaited RPG that seems fairly similar to Genshin Impact at first. But it has a much more elaborate character creation system and entirely different gameplay. Its gacha system is a little bit different from what one might expect at first glance, too. However, once you understand it, you'll realise it's pretty intuitive and simple.

When it comes to picking the best, the ToF tier list we've created will expand on why the top tier picks earned their spot, so make sure to read their description below as well (if you aren't sure why a certain weapon is in the tier we've placed it in).

So, without further ado, let's check out our Tower of Fantasy tier list!

Zoey is a Physical/Flame hyper-carry who needs screen time to pull off her highest damage. You swap to her after setting up your buffers, using her spellbook Rosebud to stack domain fields and trigger massive discharge bursts

Premier Frost carry equipped with her signature Fairy Wreath weapon. Highly potent off-field deployable mechanics allow her to dish out massive AoE Frost damage without hogging field time, enabling quick-swap rotations.

Amazing frost carry with insane movement. That said, she’s mechanically demanding, it will take some time to get use to her kit. She needs 1-star. If you can make her 3-stars go for it. Salidy

Salidy is the newest Flame carry. Her kit is designed to shred shields and provide massive burst. Veronika

Veronika is a top‑tier SSR Volt‑Frost DPS in Tower of Fantasy. She plays fast and aggressive with combo chains, extra attacks from Ballista cards/Reload points, and huge burst damage Nanto

Nanto hits hard with burst damage and really shines in late‑game boss fights and tough exploration. His kit dishes out a ton of damage, so he’s a strong pick in both PvE and PvP. Most players see him as one of the top characters right now.

Arguably the best unit in the current meta as she combines top DPS with shield penetration, crowd control, and healing. Top pick for pretty much every type of content.

Lachesis is a great new support character. Her main job isn't just healing; it's making her teammates way stronger with powerful buffs. She's especially useful for tackling the game's hardest content.

Helena is a top‑tier DPS carry whose specialty is shield breaking and high AoE damage.

Hipper's a powerful new damage dealer who melts enemies with lightning and ice, but she's expensive to build and takes serious skill to play well.

Strong attacks (Astral Slash, Meteor Rush), plus invincibility and team damage immunity. Great for team builds, high damage, and tanky support. King - Scythe of the Crow

King is an amazing character who can shatter the opponent's shield and apply a damage-over-time effect. He also possesses one of the highest default attacks in the game. Of course, he is the main DPS unit that can also deal AoE damage to surrounding units, easily landing him at the very top of our Tower of Fantasy tier list amongst the best weapons. Nemesis - Venus

Nemesis can be an outstanding support unit that has the ability to heal up and further boost the damage dealt by attacks. She can deal AoE damage as well and provide useful heals to the entire team. Nemesis is currently one of the best supporters in Tower of Fantasy. Samir - Dual EM Stars

Samir, similar to King, has truly amazing DPS, which can shred through the enemies. She can paralyse and electrocute them, which further causes them to be unable to receive buffs. The overall damage potential of Samir is only outshone by the ability to fast-chain the skills, which can obliterate opponents extremely quickly. Crow - Thunderblades

Crow plays a very decent role when it comes to crowd control since his abilities not only deal a lot of damage but also can knock back opponents and paralyse them. He can also inflict more damage to low HP opponents while reducing the damage he takes.

Claudia can be an extremely fast damage dealer who can go invisible, and while she is able to greatly boost her damage output, she can also be fairly useful to the entire team. She works amazingly with Shiro and Nemesis, since that lineup can basically unlock her full potential. Cobalt-B - Flaming Revolver

Nan Yi (released in version 3.4) is a simulacrum that can be used both as a damage carry and a support. Her versatility makes her a valuable asset to have as she can fit in almost any team. Not only does she deal a good amount of damage to the enemies, but she also grapples them and buffs her allies.

Brevey is the latest Volt / Frost Benediction that was released on patch 3.5. She's arguably the best Support currently in the game. Meryl Ironheart

Meryl is a Vault character that can be used as a main DPS or a sub DPS. She has a variety of skills that can be used to deal damage, buff her team, and control the battlefield

Lana is a flexible Altered who helps from off‑field—she still does decent damage herself but mainly boosts the team with frequent assist hits and buffs. You can swap her element with the Evolution Cube; Cocoritter - Absolute Zero

With the ability to freeze enemies, heal and support allies, Cocoritter is one of the top-tier supports currently in the game, only beaten by Nemesis. She can create an area to fully heal allies, and, when using Swift Deliverance, she can also fully clear the user of all debuffs. However, she still has some flaws, and currently belongs just a bit lower than the top of the tier list. Tsubasa - Icewind Arrow

Tsubasa can stack up damage, increasing it by quite a lot. Once unleashed, she can inflict deadly shots while applying freeze and frostbite onto enemies. If she hits an enemy's weak point or lands a headshot, she can further boost the damage dealt to the target. Frigg - Balmung

Nola is a versatile physical DPS character. Her ability to choose any of the five elements grants her access to a variety of skills and abilities. She has a powerful ground attack chain and mobility, and she's overall a formidable force on the battlefield. While she can be challenging to master, Nola's strength and versatility make her a valuable addition to any team.

Asurada's main weapon, Hellfire, deals constant damage, and he summons afterimages to deal massive damage. His gameplay involves dodging, attacking, and using his afterimages to unleash powerful combos. He's a great choice for a fire team.

Huma ignites opponents and deals damage over time, but she can also knock the target back and gain damage reduction. Overall, she's a solid team tank if the situation requires one. Huma also has fairly short cooldowns, making her a good pick for certain scenarios. Ming Jing (Zeke) - Onyx Tortoise Attached Product Images

Ming Jing, also known as Zeke, is described as an unknown visitor from outside, and Domain 9 has welcomed this man with no past. He is often associated with the Onyx Tortoise, the weapon he wields. The Onyx Tortoise is an SSR-class greatsword with wide blades that can slash through foes. It is believed that the sword is too heavy to be picked up by mere mortals. Meryl - Rosy Edge

A tank hybrid with the ability to heal and inflict damage, Meryl can be quite fun to play in situations that require you to play something that needs some resistance or immunity to crowd control, as well as sustain. Zero - Negating Cube

Zero is a utility character that reduces the healing received by enemies, reducing their speed as well while granting allies and himself immunity. He can also heal allies, making him a versatile character. He is very viable, although he is officially in the middle of our ToF tier list. Shiro - Chakram of the Seas

Shiro is a Physical DPS unit that can cause lots of damage in short succession, being able to reset cooldowns and boost the damage dealt by allies.

Berry is a Physical/Flame support DPS unit that provides buffs to physical damage teams and sustain through healing on skill attacks. She excels when paired with fist-based main DPS like Nantou, offering team damage increases through her four-piece matrice set and final damage bonuses. Best performance achieved at A3 advancement for resistance shredding in end-game content, though her standalone damage output is underwhelming compared to dedicated DPS units. Recommended for team synergy rather than as a primary damage dealer.

She is a DPS unit that can apply grievous effects on the target, causing them to take additional damage. Can work well in some situations, but overall is not something you want to use constantly. Ene - Pummeler

Ene can taunt enemies and reduce the damage received, making her a pretty solid tank. She can also inflict crowd control effects, which makes her pretty good in situations that require you to have a front-line unit that can withstand an attack, or simply if you want to slow down the opponents with well-placed stuns. Pepper - Staff of Scars

Pepper can heal allies and has a decent dodge chance, automatically triggering said healing effect. She can also inflict some crowd control effects.

Can briefly paralyse the target, has a chance to grant allies attack boosting buffs (highly dependent on the chance to shatter the opponent's shield) - not too reliable in the long run. Hilda - The Terminator

Hilda can freeze the target and reduce their weapon charge rate, but even with all the damage increases granted by her skills, her damage output is still a little bit lacklustre in the long run. Can do well in the early stages of the game, though.

That's our complete tier list for Tower of Fantasy, with every weapon ranked! Do you have anything to add? Please leave a comment below!

#4164. Infinity Nikki ushers in the Year of the Horse with... a deer-themed Version 2.2

Chromatic Beings Everbright, the latest major Infinity Nikki update, has arrived, bringing Chinese New Year celebrations vibe to the game.

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another big content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright. The latest update brings the game up to version 2.2, and introduces a new narrative chapter, and gameplay taking place around a festival narrative.

If you couldn’t guess already, the new theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

The big new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

These are doled out through Character Tokens, which are used to assign roles to each individual. The story follows Nikki as she uncovers the script that runs the realm and the facade it props up. Nikki will help free Chromafaces and dispel the illusion.

The Wanxiang Realm is split into three areas. Cai Ye is your typical lantern-lit district, where festivals and fireworks happen. Kongming Gorge is almost the opposite of that; a quiet and cold place. Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

The other big addition in 2.2 are the two new 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

Chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a new Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

As with every major update, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

If you’re jumping back into the game soon, be sure to hit up our Infinity Nikki codes page for some freebies.

#4163. Dead Cells weapons tier list - every weapon ranked

Not sure which melee weapon, ranged weapon, grenade, turret, or trap to bring? We've got you covered.

Updated on November 18th, 2026 - Version 3.5.15

Dead Cells has a lot of weapons, making it perfect for a tier list ranking every weapon. Throughout the game, you'll come across melee weapons, ranged weapons, traps, turrets, and even grenades, each with different effects like damage over time or freezing an enemy in their place. It can feel a little overwhelming, even though they're often slow or difficult to unlock and discover.

That's where our Dead Cells weapons tier list comes in. While we haven't gone into detail about most of the weapons here, we wanted to give you a quick overview of the best, the brightest, and, of course, most destructive tools in your arsenal to help you survive this perilous world.

Which weapons should you unlock in Dead Cells? It's a tough question, isn't it? You only have limited cells to spend on unlocking blueprints, so picking the best weapons to unlock can be tricky and overwhelming. We recommend starting with our S-tier weapons and working your way down from there. Most are ranked by their base damage numbers, but where a weapon or skill does something special and interesting, we've made sure to note it.

Of course, ultimately, it all comes down to personal preference. Make sure you read every weapon's description and decide if it would suit you. Some weapons have extra effects like applying a damage-over-time effect, like Bleed, or even combining with other weapons to create a one-two punch kind of effect. It's all personal. Dead Cells weapons tier list So, without further ado, let's get down to business. We've taken the time to break everything down by type for you: melee weapons, ranged weapons, shields (yes, they count), turrets and traps, and grenades. Each has its place in battle. Each will help you in some way to reach the end of the road.

If you disagree with anything on this list, then please let us know in the comments! These are a matter of opinion, after all, aside from their ranking on base damage. Critical damage is also important, so be sure to read the weapon description to take that into account.

Melee weapons make up the bread and butter of your arsenal, comprising everything from swords and axes to a spiked wrecking ball and a giant shark. Yes, a shark. Here, we've gone through and listed every melee weapon, ranked according to base damage.

Some weapons stand out more than others, of course. The Ferryman's Lantern allows you to kill an enemy to gather its soul. Then, as a secondary attack, charge it to fire those souls as projectiles, dealing critical hits if three souls are shot at the same time. With a base damage of 164 plus secondary damage of 107, then critical hits applying 429 damage, this is a monster of a weapon.

Others stand out for their usefulness and fun factor. With the Maw of the Deep, your third attack throws the shark, rooting the enemy and inflicting bleed. Rooted targets will then take critical damage - 158 base, and 270 critical.

The Rapier allows you to critical hit immediately after a roll or parry, and if you play the game like us, you'll be rolling around a lot anyway. With the Meat Skewer, your first attack places you behind the enemy, with your second hit applying critical damage. The Pure Nail comes courtesy of fellow Metroidvania Hollow Knight, allowing you to attack while moving left, right, and up. Drop down on an enemy and attack downwards to "bounce," just like in Hollow Knight, applying damage while in the air.

Finally, the Hard Light Sword is actually two weapons in one, along with the Hard Light Gun. A reference to the acclaimed Hyper Light Drifter, these weapons work in tandem. Fire the Hard Light Gun into enemies to damage and mark them. Then, the Hard Light Sword deals critical damage based on the number of shots it has received. Sword hits also recharge ammo for the gun, which (unlike other ranged weapons, more on those next) doesn't recharge over time. It's an elegant dance that might not be the most powerful, but is undoubtedly one of the most fun tools in the Dead Cells weapons arsenal.

Time for the first of our tier lists, then! Here we go: Rank Weapon S Ferryman's Lantern, Cursed Sword, War Spear, Tombstone, Flint, Oven Axe, Wrecking Ball, Giantkiller, Vampire Killer, Bible, Alucard's Sword, Death's Scythe, Misericorde A Toothpick, Symmetrical Lance, Shrapnel Axes, Hattori's Katana, Meat Skewer, Broadsword, Impaler, Crowbar, Twin Daggers, Hayabusa Boots, Vorpan, Shovel, Maw of the Deep, Rapier, Baseball Bat, Nutcracker, Pure Nail, Morning Star, Whip Sword, Sewing Scissors B Balanced Blade, Flashing Fans, Spite Sword, Rusty Sword, Bone, Swift Sword, Frantic Sword, Iron Staff, Assassin's Dagger, Rhythm n' Bouzouki, Seismic Strike, Wrenching Whip, Oiled Sword, Hayabusa Gauntlets, Blood Sword, Panchaku, Gold Digger, Machete and Pistol, Hard Light Sword, Giant Comb C Flawless, Sadist's Stiletto, Valmont's Whip, Torch, Abyssal Trident, Hand Hook, Spiked Boots, Bladed Tonfas, Dagger of Profit, Snake Fangs, Scythe Claw, Tentacle, King Scepter, Queen's Rapier, Starfury, Spartan Sandals

Ranged weapons are extremely helpful in Dead Cells, especially when you don't want to get close to an enemy. Most use ammunition that regenerates over time, or can be retrieved from enemies on death or following a successful parry, in the case of arrows. Some, like the combined Hard Light Sword and Gun mentioned on the previous page, have a special function - in this case, ammo doesn't recharge passively and instead must be recharged by landing hits with the Hard Light Sword.

Here's how we ranked the Dead Cells tier list for ranged weapons. Rank Weapon S Money Shooter, Ice Crossbow, Throwable Objects, Heavy Crossbow, Multiple-nocks Bow, Sonic Carbine, Barrel Launcher, Fire Blast, Magic Missiles, Medusa's Head, Anathema, Laser Glaive A Chakram of the Queen, The Boy's Axe, Peril Glyphs, Boomerang, Explosive Crossbow, Bow and Endless Quiver, Repeater Crossbow, Quick Bow, Laser Glaive, Gilded Yumi, Blowgun, Marksman's Bow, Ice Shards, Cross, Throwing Axe B Electric Whip, Lightning Bolt, War Javelin, Pyrotechnics, Nerves of Steel, Infantry Bow, Killing Deck, Hemorrhage C Beginner's Bow, Frost Blast, Ice Bow Firebrands, Hokuto's Bow, Magic Bow, Throwing Knife, Alchemic Carbine

Shields might be a boring choice for your adventure through Dead Cells, but don't sleep on them. Hold down a shield's assigned button to hold it up after 0.37 seconds. Attacks that hit the front are reduced by the shield's damage absorption percentage, typically around 75%, while also dealing damage to the enemy by the damage number listed on the shield.

Shields can also be used to parry attacks. Tap the button rather than hold it down, and it attempts a parry. If no attack hits during that window, you can't block or parry again for a little under a second. If your parry is successful, then a few things can happen: you can parry or block again immediately and enjoy an additional effect, depending on the attack.

Carrying a shield also passively creates a force field for 0.5 seconds after you take damage, absorbing most damage except DoT effects like poison and some enemy attacks.

Here, we've ranked shields in Dead Cells by their base block damage, meaning the damage the enemy takes after you block an attack. As always, read the shield's in-game description for any interesting effects, like AoE damage. Rank Weapon S Spiked Shield, Greed Shield, Punishment, Knockback Shield, Alucard's Shield A Force Shield, Thunder Shield, Assault Shield, Front Line Shield, Ice Shield B Rampart, Bloodthirsty Shield C Old Wooden Shield, Cudgel, Parry Shield

Deployable skills in Dead Cells come in three forms: traps and turrets, grenades, and various miscellaneous powers. It isn't possible to start with these skills without the Recycling Tubes upgrade.

First, let's cover deployable skills like traps and turrets. These come in powered and unpowered forms. Powered skills, such as turrets, need you to remain within their proximity for them to function. Line of sight is best, with the effective radius decreased if blocked by terrain. As long as you're within proximity, though, you'll notice a line of electricity connecting you to the deployed skill, allowing it to function.

Unpowered deployable skills are typically traps that don't actively attack on your behalf, such as traps that activate when the enemy steps onto them.

Let's rank the various types of deployable skills. First up, turrets. The Sinew Slicer is particularly worth noting. You'll come across it early, and it makes short work of early enemies without placing you in danger. Rank Skill S Barnacle, Scavenged Bombard, Heavy Turret, Cleaver A Double Crossb-o-matic, Sinew Slicer B Tesla Coil C Flamethrower Turret

Next up, traps and miscellaneous powers. The Emergency Door skill simply spawns a door in front of you, which acts like a regular door, meaning it can be destroyed to stun enemies on the other side. The Night Light is extremely situational and can be deployed in the Forgotten Sepulcher to help with the Darkness. Requiring 120 seconds to recharge, it can be thrown to a location to create a temporary light at that location. Touch it to replenish your light aura. Rank Skill S Crusher A Explosive Decoy B Wolf Trap C Night Light, Emergency Door

Grenades in Dead Cells do exactly what you expect: they explode. What more could you want? Simply throw, and enjoy! Some have added effects, of course, and can be paired with other skills or weapons for greater use. The Ice Grenade freezes enemies, for example, and the Root Grenade roots enemies, causing damage over time and keeping them rooted. The Magnetic Grenade is useful in crowded rooms. After a few moments, it attracts enemies in a large area, then explodes to deal electrical damage over time.

Grenades, like other skills, aren't exactly consumables as you would expect in other games. Rather they each have a set cooldown, meaning they can be reused over and over again.

The Hunter's Grenade is situational, which is why it's ranked C, but it's quite useful at the same time. Throw it to "annoy" a monster. When its health drops to 40% or less, use "Blueprint Extractor" to grab a blueprint. Rank Skill S Powerful Grenade, Holy Water A Infantry Grenade, Cluster Grenade, Magnetic Grenade B Stun Grenade, Ice Grenade, Fire Grenade, Root Grenade, Oil Grenade, Swarm C Hunter's Grenade

#4162. Zenelss Zone Zero Version 2.6 has you playing as an event planner and social media manager for an idol group

Zenelss Zone Zero's Encore for an Old Dream has a good excuse for introducing some new mechanics to the action game.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered a tonne of information about the game’s big upcoming update, Version 2.6. This latest addition kicks off celebrations in New Eridu, and it’s dubbed Encore for an Old Dream.

Version 2.6 is not far off, either, arriving in ZZZ on February 6 - exactly one week from today. Encore for an Old Dream is something of an in-between story that takes place after the end of Season 2.

The narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for New Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day. At the centre of the celebrations is the debut of idol group Angels of Delusion at the 404 Error music venue, but not all is as it seems.

The story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with new maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

Angels of Delusion is also the group that the two new Agents being introduced in this update belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

Sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

Aria is the other new arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

Version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a new game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

Beyond all the celebrations, this update also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

The big event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

As always, there’s no reason not to catch up on the latest set of Zenless Zone Zero codes for some free in-game items.

#4161. GTA 6: Where to Find Strip Clubs

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

Who doesn’t like to party a little in games? Well, Grand Theft Auto 6 certainly has various means to do so. Whether it’s a club, a fancy VIP experience, or a traditional strip club, Vice City has everything you’re looking for.

This has been a staple of the series ever since Grand Theft Auto 3, as going into these clubs not only facilitated story missions but also allowed the characters (and the player) to get an NSFW experience. There are a handful of different options in Rockstar’s Grand Theft Auto 6, but finding them can be a bit tricky. Most of them are centralized, and some you won’t see until much later in the campaign.

Players already have a list of 61 cheats to look forward to.

The first strip club you’ll find is in Chapter 2 upon meeting Vicki who will introduce you to her boss at the Delights Cabaret. This is a traditional strip club, but one that’s more in line with being out in the middle of nowhere. It’s more of a bar atmosphere with girls in the back.

With that said, you’ll be able to find Delights Cabaret in the Port Gellhorn section of the map, all the way to the west.

The first strip club you’ll come across in Vice City is part of the story between Jason and his old buddy Dre’Quan. He will invite you out to his club, where he will introduce you to Boobie, who will be putting Jason and Lucia up in his apartment.

This is a traditional strip club, with dancers on poles. It’s also one of the more expensive clubs, with VIP dance treatments costing $1,000. Jack of Hearts is located in central Crosstown, just south of your apartment. This is the go-to spot for adult entertainment.

This has more of a club vibe with a bit of stripping. It’s far fancier than Jack of Hearts, but has just as many options, if not more, with dancing on the dancefloor. The best part is that the VIP dances will only set you back $300 in-game.

NINE1NINE is south of Jack of Hearts, at the top of the Downtown section of the map. Even when you roll up to the place for the first time, you’ll notice just how much nicer it is, with a more exclusive feeling.

This is less of a strip club and more of a dance club. At least one main mission takes place here, and it’s probably the best place to go dancing with Lucia. It features multiple rooms with different types of music and DJs, and its aesthetic is built around an old vault, with a giant vault door at the entrance.

It’s definitely somewhere to check out in Vice City, and thankfully, it’s right across the street from NINE1NINE, just to the west.

Last but not least is VYB. It’s located in the northeast portion of Ocean Beach, directly south of your Act 4 home in Washington Beach. Similar to The Vault, it has a more traditional club atmosphere, with dance floors and high-class bars in the back.

Unfortunately, VYB isn’t accessible to the public, as it’s part of Dre’Quan’s lengthy story and is only used during a main mission in Act 4. With that said, it’s probably the nicest club in the game.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

#4159. Starsand Island is a life and farming sim that isn't gacha, and it's out next week

Starsand Island officially has an Early Access release date, and it sounds like it won't stay there for years.

Though it may seem like we just had a big life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

The game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Seed Sparkle Lab announced today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

The developer said to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access

Starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab says you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

You can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

#4157. Nioh 3 launches, immediately becomes the most played Nioh ever on Steam

Just a few hours after launch, Nioh 3 is already the biggest release in series history on Steam.

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

This already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is currently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

There are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

#4154. GTA 6: Best Ways to Make Money

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

Money makes the world go round, and that certainly is the case for Grand Theft Auto 6. This is one of, if not the biggest game to ever be released, and in order to make it big in the massive world Rockstar has established, you need to take on some jobs. Some are shady while others are slightly less shady.

Most require some sort of crime, but for the most part, it’s not too difficult to earn millions by the end of the adventure. This guide will help you make money from the early stages of the game to the late stages. For example, the first two chapters only has a couple of ways to make money, while the end game has a slew of options, but only one that’s worth it.

Players already have a list of 61 cheats to look forward to.

For the first chapter, it’s primarily doing side activities such as Kenton’s scuba treasure dives or ripping off the Kingfishers gangs. Both pay decently for early game adventures and encounters.

By far the best way to make money in the second chapter, and really throughout the entire game, is stealing cars and selling them. Early in the game, you’ll only have access to some cheaper vehicles, so look out for any type of van that might be hauling some items, such as a news van. These will generally net you above $1,000. It’s a start.

When you get to Vice City, you will meet a man named Randy who wants some very nice cars, and in order to do this, you will need to obtain the ability to clone a key. Thankfully, he shows you, and you can earn a lot of money with him. The downside is that the higher the price on the car, the more likely it’ll have an Advanced Tracker, which is a pain to deal with. It’s almost better to go with mid-payout vehicles with Standard Trackers and drive carefully, which will net you a condition bonus.

This is technically good in the early stages of the game, but when you get halfway through the campaign, you’ll likely have access to more hardware, faster getaway vehicles and body armor. At this point, you’ll have some cash put aside to get the job done easier, so take advantage of this.

Another means of getting paid is ripping off gangs. There will be various set-ups all throughout Vice City and the northern region with a decent pay day. They will also have key valuables that can be sold for quite a bit, on top of unique weapons and cars that you might want to add to your personal collection.

When you get into the five couple of chapters, there will be some very good opportunities to make some real money. As you learn through the campaign, you need more and more money, and bank robberies are the endgame ways to make money. This is because, while you can take on small banks for upwards of $20,000, some of the big banks can make upwards of ten times that.

The problem is that these are very difficult to overcome. You will need to ensure everyone stays in line and no bank alarms go off too early. Then there’s getting away from the cops, which can be challenging. But if you’re able to do it, the pay is worth it.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

#4153. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026) Review - Exceptionally Familiar

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64 is the most important video game ever made… to me. My byline would not appear in the pages of Game Informer without my original experience playing that game. But it is nearly 30 years old, and despite establishing many important staples of 3D gaming, its age is becoming more apparent. Ocarina of Time was due for a re-examination, and its remake is a wonderful recreation of the 1998 experience with improvements on basically every element: visuals, storytelling, timeless design, and more. It is, however, a remake, and the coloring (though expertly done) is firmly inside the lines.

Ocarina of Time is gorgeous. That the game is less than 25 GB is an engineering marvel. I never quite came around to the odd looks of child Link or Zelda, but every other character, environment, enemy, item, and boss looks incredible. I eagerly looked forward to meeting every weirdo in Hyrule to see their new look, and was never disappointed. The ReDeads and Stalchildren are more traumatic than ever, and every NPC childhood crush I thought I had moved on from was reignited. Watching the sun rise and set over Hyrule feels as magical as it did in the past.

The same accolades can be awarded to the soundtrack. The new orchestrations are incredible, and watching Link’s 4K fingers play the proper notes on his ocarina is mesmerizing. Nintendo continues to fumble voice acting with stiff performances, but thankfully the vast majority of dialogue – one of the primary changes in this remake – is not spoken. Characters don’t necessarily have more to say, but what they say is more impactful, and there are a handful of small but exciting expansions to character and story details. Nothing is groundbreaking or changes how you look at familiar elements, but it manages to be simultaneously nostalgic and improved.

And that’s the closest I got to what I would debatably call a problem: It all looks new, but doesn’t feel particularly new. Ocarina’s overall design holds up. The time travel element is surprising and creates great opportunities to see the world change and evolve; puzzles and their solutions are rewarding; the basics of combat, though simple, are thrilling. All those elements have been adjusted, but not overhauled. Dungeons and their puzzles have been tweaked to remove annoyances (such as fewer keys in the Water Temple), and the new swordplay effects make connecting your blade to monsters feel incredible. But they’re all ultimately small changes that don’t cast Ocarina in a new light or consider its history. It’s a straightforward recreation. But an admittedly very good one.

The biggest, most impactful changes are the new full camera control and active jumping. Swinging the camera around to take a closer look at the upgraded environments is genuinely stirring, especially in the locations that used to be pre-rendered. There is an undefined and exclusive-to-video games emotion I experienced often while trekking locations I thought I knew so well, only to realize I have never seen or looked at it in this way, and I chased and captured that feeling all over Hyrule. Jumping may seem small, but it made me a more active participant in exploration. It also has the benefit of making some encounters feel somewhat trivial (turns out being able to jump over Blade Traps really diminishes their threat), and I was just fine with that.

The beautiful 2026 version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time does not study the legacy or impact of the landmark game on the video game medium. Instead, it is a meticulous and incredibly impressive recreation of one of the best games ever made. I was rarely surprised during my playthrough, but I was incredibly excited to see old friends and I happily share without embarrassment that playing through its final hour made me cry. For many like me, the original Ocarina of Time is an impactful adventure that arrived at a time in their lives when magic still felt real. Playing the game again 28 years later and appreciating the care taken to maintain and improve that original vision was the ultimate surprise of the whole experience: I didn’t expect to be so moved.

Alex Van Aken contributed to this article.

#4152. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

Honkai: Star Rail's next major update introduces a whole new planet to the RPG, and way more besides.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big new world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

If you log in after launch, you’ll get 20 free pulls and a new free outfit for Ruan Mei. If you play while the Yao Guang fortune event is active, you could earn 1,600 Stellar Jades. You can also expect a free 5-Star character selector to arrive at some point after launch, giving you a free choice between popular (but admittedly a bit old for the meta these days) limited-banner characters Jing Yuan, Kafka, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, Jingliu, Sparkle, Acheron, and Aventurine.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

While some will appear on Jason’s property right away, most are tied to shops within the game or are found after certain events further into the story, some of which are only available basically at the end. With that said, this will hopefully give you a good idea where to find everything.

Players already have a list of 61 cheats to look forward to.

These are the first two vehicles you’ll have access to outside of Jason’s Ganado muscle car after you start the game. They will be conveniently placed near Jason’s house in Chapter 1 to take for a ride.

The Ganado Retro Build is one of the first Ultimate Edition item you can get in your campaign, and it’s the easiest. All you will need to do, starting in Chapter 1, is drive into a Pay ‘N’ Spray with Jason’s Ganado, which will be impounded past Chapter 2, and go into Complete Kits. The first option should be the Retro Build, which upgrades Jason’s wheels decently, at least for a starter vehicle.

There are a couple of revolvers ready to be picked up at an Ammu-Nation locker whenever Lucia gains access to them starting in Chapter 2. These are powerful guns that should be put in your arsenal.

On top of that, there are weapon variants for a handful of guns, such as the Girardi ES9 and Klose K17, which can be customized at a locker whenever you see fit. These will upgrade the two weapons nicely.

This is technically available at the beginning of the game, but you likely won’t come up to the shopping district that houses this store until Chapter 3. This is located within Vice City’s southern portion of the map and has some rather nice new clothes for you to pick up. The downside is that you have to bye them in-game.

Hair is an important feature, so why not hit up Sara’s Unisex Salon? The signature hair is found at every salon in the game, but the unique hairstyles are located in Hamlet starting in Chapter 1. This is located relatively close to the correctional facility.

This is the first boat you’ll be able to own, but it’s only available in Chapter 4. As soon as you move into your new apartment and kick off the chapter, there will be a new icon immediately to the northwest. You’ll find the boat here at the Washington Bach canal dock.

One of the most iconic cars in GTA Vice City, you’re able to pick up this vehicle much later in the game, specifically in Chapter 5 at the Pegassi Residences.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

#4145. God Of War Laufey Delayed To May

PlayStation first-party developer Santa Monica Studio has delayed its upcoming action game, God of War Laufey, to May. More specifically, the PlayStation 5-exclusive title will now launch on May 20, representing a roughly three-month delay from the original February 16 release date.

"Since the reveal of God of War Laufey in June, we've been deeply grateful to see so much excitement for Faye's journey through the Everywhen," a statement from the studio reads. "We don't take for granted the trusted place in the studio to make an extraordinary experience worthy of the passion and dedication of our fans. With this in mind, we've made the decision to delay God of War Laufey's release to May 20, 2027. We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential. On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon."

God of War Laufey stars Faye, Kratos' deceased wife from his Norse adventures, after she ends up in the mysterious realm known as the Everywhen following her death. There, she will fight monsters and creatures from various mythologies alongside a talking gelatinous cube and a talking sword sash. We'll have to wait a bit longer than expected now to see what her adventure entails.

God of War Laufey will now launch on PS5 next year on May 20. In the meantime, check out this newly revealed weapon, then read about how Amazon's God of War TV series has recast Kratos as Dave Bautista.

It is also, quite visibly, the most popular Nioh release ever on PC, and it was impressive watching more and more players jump into the game over the weekend and push the numbers higher.

That’s an incredibly healthy player base, but more than that, it’s more than double the previous record holder, Nioh 2, which peaked at 41,325 concurrent players in 2021. Steam players appear to be very happy with the game, too, with over 1,560 reviews and an overall Very Positive rating.

#4142. Love and Deepspace ushers in the Year of the Horse with a Wuxia-inspired AU multi-banner and a restaurant management mini-game

A new Love and Deepspace banner event is here with a lot of rewards to earn, and brand-new Memories for all five lads to unlock.

Love and Deepspace has kicked off the next big in-game moment and is celebrating Chinese New Year with the arrival of a new 5-Star Memory Series. This year's spring-themed banner is available now until February 27, and it comes with a host of events.

The Mortality’s Tenderness banner features five new limited-time 5-Star Memories, one each for the game’s five love interests. The theme is all about warmth, reunion, and intimacy, taking place in a Wuxia-inspired setting that's once again an alternate universe from the main story of the game.

The new memory cards are Xavier: Blades with Blossoms, Zayne: Entwined Kites, Rafayel: Carved Gemheart, Sylus: Shared Lanterns, and Caleb: Clearday Return. You can pick three of the five to focus on and further pick one to guarantee on your second 5-star pull; and you can earn wish rewards by making cumulative wishes over the course of the event.

Some of the rewards you could get include limited headwear, Limited Deepspace Wishes, and — of course — Memory-themed outfits and hairstyles inspired by the new Memories. Outside of wish rewards, the Memory Series comes with growth tasks that rewards you with in-game materials for levelling up the new cards during the event. When you reach Rank 1 for any new Memory from the banner, you’ll earn a Memory-themed outfit with a special colour that matches your chosen love interest.

Illusio returns as part of the new event, too, letting you customise the look of Kindled Moments across all five new Memories. Things you can customise include selecting the outfits and accessories for each love interest, so you can recreate Kindled Moments in your own style. As always, Kindled Moments will go back to their default look after the event ends.

There’s a new mini-game to play, too, available only during the event. It’s called Courteous Fare, a frantic but familiar restaurant management simulation that allows you to unlock a variety of rewards.

Furthermore, if you log in for 10 days throughout the event, you can unlock a new outfit set, Wealth Overflow, which can be worn by any of the love interests as well as the heroine. There are other login rewards, too, like 10 Deepspace Wishes, 10 Empyrean Wishes, His and My Outfit sets, two dynamic portrait photo poses, and loads more.

Finally, the Golden Fortune event adds even more daily log in rewards in the form of one free "shake" per day, from which you can earn a random reward of between 68 and 108 Diamonds — that adds up to a total of 1,296 Diamonds if you show up every day.

#4141. Zelda Ocarina Remake Producers Talk Changing And Maintaining The Game, Easter Eggs, The Bombchu Bowling Alley Operator, And More

Today marks the release of the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2. You can read my full, positive review here. Ahead of the game’s release, but after having played the game to completion (well… 99% as you will learn below), I traveled to New York to speak with Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma (whose work on the original Ocarina of Time marked his first involvement with the series) and Ocarina of Time remake producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi (director of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom among other Zelda titles).

Topics include how the team approached remaking Ocarina of Time, what needed changing and what needed to stay the same, their thoughts on the Easter Eggs from the original game, the fate and marital status of the Bombchu Bowling girl, and more.

The discussion covers a fairly faithful remake of Ocarina of Time for Nintendo 64, which launched nearly 30 years ago, but I have spoiler-marked certain questions and answers that might be considered sensitive if you want to maintain surprise when playing the remake yourself.

Mr. Fujibayashi, what is your relationship to Ocarina of Time?

Fujibayashi: Regarding the original Ocarina of Time, at the time I was working for a different company, so it was mainly me as an end user trying to looking forward to the experience of what a 3D Zelda is going to look like. So, really, I was just waiting in anticipation for that.

How long has the remake been in development?

Aonuma: It's actually kind of hard to say exactly when development began because the earliest thought process was us thinking about the 40th anniversary of The Legend of Zelda approaching, and so we started to have this conversation, “Oh, what should we make to mark this occasion?” And then at that point, we decided on Ocarina of Time, and so a lot of time elapsed from the beginning of that conversation about the anniversary until we got to Ocarina. So it's hard to pinpoint exactly when the development itself began.

Was this a more relaxing game to develop after making Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom back-to-back?

Aonuma: Was it relaxing? That's kind of a hard question to ask. I would say it's more a different style of development. So, if we looked at Tears of the Kingdom, Breath of the Wild, these were created as new games with a very different kind of development cycle. Whereas for a remake like this one, we decided to take an interesting approach, which is to bring in this new younger staff and find out what they would bring to this project in terms of their own experience, their own interpretation as newer staff.

And so my role here was really advising them on this, and it's not always like the development cycle of a new game. But in one sense, the producer has to be careful not to advise too much, to say that you must do it like this. You don't want to prescribe the approach that anyone is going to take. You want to make sure that there's enough space for these younger staff members to have their own interpretation, their own approach to it.

Do you have remake philosophies or rules, like what needs to stay the same and what should change?

Fujibayashi: So, in fact, there were pretty clear kind of rules or guidelines, as you said. First, is because you know, as Mr. Aonuma had mentioned, where he wanted to, the development team was centered around the young directors that took part in this development. And when we first started discussing what kind of game and what kind of approach you wanted to take. One thing that really came through and we clarified was, as you mentioned, what are we going to change and what are we going to keep the same.

And I'll start with what we wanted to change, and that was really to make sure that – because we have the ability to use the latest technology through the Nintendo Switch 2 – there's a lot we can change and improve upon, such as you know obviously things like controls, graphics. We also have a new controller, so that allows for the new camera controls. And we’re really able to fine tune and polish the feel of the game and there was excitement for all the ways of expression we can provide the player.

But on the other hand, thinking about what we didn't want to change, we were thinking about the creators of the original Ocarina of Time, and what they wanted to convey, the experience that they wanted to provide for users and players through this title. That's something that we wanted to keep intact and that spirit to carry across. And we wanted to make sure that this new game is able to deliver that in the way that we wanted them to.

Aonuma: So speaking as someone who worked on the original Ocarina of Time for Nintendo 64, you always have those moments looking back of, “Oh, you know, I really wanted to do more of this,” or, “I wanted to be able to express this in a different way,” but you're faced with certainly the tech limitations of the time. And I went on from Ocarina of Time to work on other Zelda franchise titles, as well. And with each new title, you're always looking for a new way to express something that may not have been available to you previously. But you always have to keep in mind is what makes a Zelda game special, and how do we protect that? How do we keep that in store for the players, as well. So, on this project in particular, I had to think of that through the lens of how do we protect the things that make it the Zelda Ocarina experience, but also how do I give the freedom to the staff to find their own expression of these ideas? And I think between those two things, we found a really good balance. So I'm very happy about that.

When we interviewed you, Mr. Aonuma, for Game Informer’s Breath of the Wild cover story, Shigeru Miyamoto was present, and he made a joke about the challenge of the water temple. Are you happy with where the Water Temple is now in the remake?

Aonuma: Certainly, looking back on the challenge level of the Water Temple, I think it was hard, but some of that came from the system that we were presenting to players. So, for example, if you look at the way that players used to have to switch to the heavy iron boots so that they could sink in the water, you had to go to a different screen and press the button. But now that we're able to give players a shortcut, single button on the gameplay screen, I think they can get to that more quickly. It's a better experience because they can focus on solving the puzzle rather than having to navigate menus and thinking about that and interrupting the flow of their thought each time.

Another consideration compared to the original is that you couldn't move the camera angle in the original game, and so if you were looking for a certain room in this 3D space relative to where you are now, it was much more difficult to orient yourself and think about the space where that room might exist. So I think those two together, you know, also with the heavy boots being one button press, I think this, for me, is the best version of the Water Temple.

Is the canon of the Zelda timeline considered at all during development? Did you think about adding in Easter eggs that made references to things that would have happened later in the Zelda story? Like Wind Waker taking place after Ocarina of Time, for example.

Aonuma: It's funny because the staff would sometimes ask me about the possibility of including nods to the timeline or references to the other game, and I actually, at the time, would say, "No, let's focus on this game. Let's make this the best version of Ocarina of Time that we can." So, the timeline was in the back of our mind, but we didn't consider taking an approach to this game where we actually, explicitly included references like that.

When testing the game, was it challenging to find people who had never played Ocarina of Time?

Aonuma: As it turns out, both on our staff and in the testing teams, there's a lot of young people, and many of them had never played the original. So it wasn't a challenge to find them.

Who do you primarily consider this remake to be for? New people who have never played Ocarina? Or fans like myself who consider it to be, frankly, their favorite game. Who is the important audience?

Fujibayashi: The answer is both. Our response to those fans who have fond memories of this title is really what I mentioned earlier: being able to provide the experience of what it was like to play Ocarina of Time back to them, and that was our response to them. And when it comes to the players that are experiencing this for the first time, whether it's the graphics, or the controls, or the ability to shift and move the camera; those are all changes and fine-tuning that we've made to make sure that people who are used to modern gaming are able to enter this experience with as little friction as possible. So again, to answer your question? It's really both.

Aonuma: Certainly, when you look at the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, there is so much hidden in the world that people spend a lot of time looking for things. And your first time playing through, you may not find all of it in one go. People in that kind of situation would refer to strategy books and information that they can find.

For example, when you're looking for the like last Skulltala and you already have 99, our job is to think about how to give the player an approach to that sort of a problem. What kind of information can we give them to help out. To make it a fun, but still challenging experience, because we want even new players to come in and to be able to fully experience this world that we've created for them, even though old fans are going to come in with a little bit of an advantage in the form of a lot of prior game knowledge.

I'm not kidding about needing some help with that final Skulltala. I'm going to hand you my Switch 2 after this so you can show me where it is because it's been driving me crazy. I've been having dreams about where the final Skulltala might be.

The end of the game in the remake made me emotional in a way I wasn't expecting. It made me cry, just the whole ending of the experience overall. Were you expecting that kind of reaction from players?

Fujibayashi: So first, I want to say I'm very, very happy and excited to hear you say that because, as you mentioned, that cutscene – cutscenes in general – but that cutscene specifically is something that we, as a dev team, heavily discussed. Because of the limitations of the technology back in the day, there might have been things that we weren't able to convey fully, whether it's because of the tempo of the game… whatever it is. And so, when we approached this remake, we wanted to make sure that we captured that moment in the way that we wanted to express it. So that the right kinds of emotions are evoked, and that we can convey the emotion and the story that we wanted to at that moment. And now that hearing you say that and kind of having that reaction really struck a chord? I'm really relieved to hear that because that's exactly what we wanted to do.

The ReDeads, the Shadow Temple, the Dead Hand miniboss, Wall Masters – these enemies traumatized a whole generation of kids. I'm curious if that was always the intention and how did you approach making sure that those elements still remained scary? Was there a line that was too scary?

Aonuma: Certainly, at the time, we had this intent to make sure that we allow the players to find the enemies a little bit scary. They have to be, right? We want to express that sort of thing. But more than anything, they are part of this Fantasy world, which has both light and dark portions, and so we're trying to bring that feeling across. It’s not that we're trying to scare people outright as the entire intent, but rather show that you know Link is part of a brighter part of the world where people are friendly, and Ganon is a part of the darker part of the world where there's a lot of scary things. And we kept that in mind in the remake as well.

We wanted to make sure we were bringing that out, but the tools that we have available to us now for expression are so capable that if we really tried, of course, we could make something that was very, very scary. But this is supposed to be for all kinds of players. We didn't want to hit the scary notes so strongly that we were putting off new players or younger players, and so we want to have that tuning very carefully in mind as we're making those adjustments in terms of presenting that final expression in the game.

I shudder to visualize what the scarier versions of the ReDeads might look like.

Aonuma: What was your experience of them this time?

Oh, terrifying! That noise. The noise they make. That scream. I feel it in my chest. It just recalls that scariness of my childhood in a way that I admit is very entertaining, and I like. Do you remember recording that sound effect? How did you do that? Did you have someone scream?

For the remake, a lot has been rewritten. The meaning hasn't been changed dramatically, but pretty much everything has been rewritten. What was the goal with the rewriting overall?

Fujibayashi: Yes, it's as you said. We did a lot of rewriting of the text. When it comes to the original Ocarina of Time, there's the idea that because it was 28 years ago – it's a long time ago – there's the turn of phrase, or the way it's been written, is sometimes not clear or doesn't work in the modern day, given the context of the modern day. And so that's why we wanted to make sure that it makes sense and it's easier to understand for people who are familiar with playing modern games, and also that it works better here.

And when you think about… obviously the graphics have been improved significantly. Before we had to do things like… “That blue ocarina that is the size that you could fit on a hand,” something like that, to make sure that the idea gets across to the player. But now, because the graphics are improved, it's very clear what the size it is. It's very clear that it's a blue ocarina. So with the new graphics, if you go through the wordy explanation of what it is, the player is going to be like, "Yeah, I can see it." So in order to make sure that we remove those kind of slight hurdles and really make sure that we can present the game and improve not only the expression but also the pacing of the game? That's something that we really took into consideration as we were rewriting the game.

I wanted to ask about some specific changes for the remake. You get five bottles now. Why?

Aonuma: Because bottles are so important to the way the player plays the game, like looking for strategies to deal with different kinds of situations, even at the time of development of the original title, I thought, “Oh, you know, I could do with even just one more bottle.” I think certainly when you collect all four in the original, you feel great about that at time. But I was still thinking like one more would be okay, right?

So, all this time that was in the back of my mind. But when the new younger staff were familiarizing themselves with the old game and thinking about what they might want to change in this version, one thing that I suggested was that the player could get their first bottle earlier, and this would actually be really useful in terms of reinforcing for the player how helpful bottles were and motivating them on their quest to find the next bottle. It strengthens that whole sequence through the game by changing the order just a little bit there. But yeah, certainly, once you have a certain number of bottles, you're going to feel a little bit more confident and more comfortable. But reinforcing that feeling early on, I think, was important for us in the development of this one.

In the original, there were Nintendo character portraits in Zelda's courtyard of Mario, Yoshi, and more, but those have been removed. I was curious as to why.

Aonuma: Certainly, at the time, when we put those there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal. Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing. But looking at it now, like if a player is coming through that area, and given the overall way that we're, you know, creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, "Why is Yoshi there?” We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time.

However, you will remember that there is one design element on Talon with Bowser on it, and that's part of the original design of the character. So we didn't change that. That stays as is.

I have some short-answer questions. The woman who runs the Bombchu Bowling game. What happened to her after seven years. And is she single?

Aonuma: That's something we're not going to touch, and I'll leave it to your imagination.

One of the Skulltala rewards is Bombchus, which I found disappointing when I was young, and I found disappointing as an adult. Why does he give you Bombchus?

Aonuma: So that feeling you had when you got, as a reward for a certain number of Skulltalas, the Bombchus, and you thought, “Wait, that's it?” That's also part of the original experience of the 64 version. So there, there's an approach that we take where we try to keep all of the different notes that people felt in the original game in place. You know, sometimes it's really remarkable, fun things, and other times it's slight moments of disappointment. Even that could be memorable in that way. It's important to maintain that.

The Great Fairies. What do they need rupees for?

Fujibayashi: You know, it's really about a feeling. It's like in Japan sometimes, like donations to a temple or something similar like that. It's to express your reverence for the great fairies.

The 3DS remake had Skyward Sword art hidden in a couple of places, but you removed it for this remake. You didn't want to keep the Skyward Sword art?

Aonuma: [Laughs] I do remember at the time the designers on the 3DS version were really interested in placing Easter Eggs like that throughout the game, and the timing of the release of Skyward Sword was such that it was perfect to go ahead and include that. So I said, “Okay, sure.” But like earlier when we were talking about in the courtyard sequence with the Yoshi portrait. You know, you don't want to interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're currently doing in the game. So for that reason, we decided not to go that way.

Mr. Fujibayashi, you directed Skyward Sword. Were you sad to see that reference removed?

Fujibayashi: [Laughs] No, it’s really as Mr. Aonuma said. There was an underlying concept in what we were going for, so no hard feelings there.

I think the biggest cutscene change in the game is when Link transitions from child to adult. It is now a much more involved sequence. Why did that scene need such a drastic change?

Aonuma: So I think that's really connected to the way we were thinking about expressing things in the original. We couldn't do everything. We couldn't express everything that we'd like to, and I think in that moment where you have Ganondorf having this reaction to Link becoming older, that cutscene in the original, it was very low on explanation.

So, you have these thoughts in the player's mind like, “Oh wait, why is he there? What's the relation to this process?” So, you want something that explains his presence, that explains his reaction to make a bigger impression on the player overall, and that's something that you can use to connect the motivation to want to face Ganondorf in the final fight. Something that I think comes across better now.

[I pulled out my Switch 2 and showed them how I was missing one Skulltala in Hyrule Field]

You can see here I have 99 out of 100 and am have two out of three in Hyrule Field. Can you point to a general location to give me an idea of where to look?

#4140. GTA 6: How to Get into Bank Vaults

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the most complex and grandiose open worlds there has ever been, and because of its name, there will be a bit of stealth. But it’s not cars you’re stealing, or at least not in this guide. Here, we are talking about Lucia and Jason finding their way into a higher payday, and to do that, they will need to rob some more advanced locations, specifically banks. With this guide, you’ll learn how to get into the vault, where all the money is kept.

So, you’re fed up with the cash from the drawers in banks and the small safes in the back rooms and want some of the bigger dough. Well, there’s only one way to do that: through the bank vaults.

Players already have a list of 61 cheats to look forward to.

Getting into a bank vault isn’t easy as it requires a lot of planning and work. Well, a little bit. Unfortunately, the first requirement in order to get into a bank vault will likely be disappointing to most people: you need to be at the end of Chapter 4. This means that you have done jobs for Yasmani in Vice City and have completed the VCIA Takedown mission, one of the biggest heists in the game.

After completing this, you will be given some time to cooldown and lie low. But for Jason and Lucia, that means finding more creative ways of robbing. Yasmani will contact you about a money truck coming around Little Cuba. Head to the Cuban Restaurant, Café Orquidea and wait. This will unlock the That’s Where the Money Is … quest.

Here you will have to tail a money truck, don't get too close until it reaches its destination: Lombank – Ocean Beach. This is one of the smaller banks in the area, having only medium security but a decent amount of take if you’re up to the challenge. Once both you and the money truck have parked, head inside and stick the place up. Head through the back door and rob the vault as it’s open thanks to the money truck making a pickup (or dropoff).

The challenging part is, because you robbed the vault, you now have four stars, which can be trouble to get away from. Thankfully, there is a dock nearby, and taking a high-speed boat out into the open waters has a greater chance of escape. Once you do, unfortunately, the island is now looking for you.

Thankfully, now that you have gotten your first taste of the vault, you’ll want more. Thankfully, Yasmani will now offer tips for when a security van is making a pickup or drop off, allowing you to time when to go shopping.

After that, all you need to do is call or visit Yasmani and you can take one of the money vaults in Vice City. Mind you, it will cost you $10,000 for the tip, but the take will be much larger. Just be prepared for some heavy gunfire.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.
