#4083. Every MTG Universes Beyond Crossover Set, Ranked

Wizards of the Coast originally released Magic: The Gathering crossovers at a slow and steady pace, but four Universes Beyond sets have dropped in 2026, meaning the floodgates have well and truly opened, for better or worse. Luckily this isn't the norm, and there will be an even split of Universes Beyond and in-universe sets moving forward, currently slated to be three of each every year.

If you're looking for a comprehensive guide to all the Universes Beyond sets and major drops, including Commander precons, listed in order from worst to best, then we've got you covered. Each set is ranked based on originality, card quality, interest in the release, and the impact of the cards on the MTG landscape (in the case of Commander/Standard set releases).

Updated on November 18, 2026 by Niall Walsh: Star Trek is out now, and it's certainly not getting the best reception from players or critics, but it brings the 2026 release schedule to a close, at least in terms of full sets. We know we have three more Universes Beyond sets coming next year, but only one has been revealed so far...

Where do we even begin with the Spider-Man set? This disaster of a release didn't even make it to MTG Arena at first because of licensing issues, which led to widespread confusion in the community. On top of that, what was supposed to be a smaller set became a full Standard release, resulting in cards that felt rushed and uninspiring and that didn't synergize well with existing Standard sets or function well as a standalone product.

The straw that broke the camel's back was the fact that this set ended up pushing back the release of Lorwyn Eclipsed, a hugely anticipated original MTG set, and it came in the middle of a major ramp-up in new products, leaving players feeling burnt out and slighted by the expectation to invest in new products so often.

Magic: The Gathering has plenty of mechanically unique cards that have only seen one printing and there's no guarantee that they'll be reprinted.

It very nearly fell to the bottom of the pile, but the Star Trek set just about manages to come in ahead of Spider-Man... for now. This list is fluid, so time may treat Star Trek worse than it did Spider-Man, but Star Trek's immediate legacy in Magic: The Gathering is a set that was almost universally panned for one reason or another.

While we had fun during prerelease, the set isn't having much impact on the Standard meta beyond a few cards like The Naked Time, and many core Magic fans disdain sets where the artwork depicts real-life actors playing roles we've seen on screen. It makes for a set that lacks creativity in the art department, and compared to sets like Reality Fracture and even The Hobbit, the gap is huge.

Availability was also a nightmare for Star Trek, with stock for the set still not with some retailers almost a week after release, which is having a knock-on effect for players.

One saving grace for Star Trek is its mechanics. Assimilate is cool, as is Strange New Worlds, and the return of Spacecrafts is welcome; if you can ignore the artwork and card names, this does have an Edge of Eternities 2 feel to it. Its Commander decks are 50/50, with the Borg and Landing Party decks being by far the strongest and most popular of the four, but that's not to say the Klingon and Federation decks are useless; they're just not as good in direct comparison.

The Universes Beyond Doctor Who release brought with it four very strong Commander decks, each one designed around several iterations of The Doctor and their villains. The main release also came with three Secret Lairs: Dalek Lands, Weeping Angels, and Regeneration.

Despite the initial reaction to these Commander decks, some have become shelf fodder and are often available below MSRP. This sometimes happens when a product just isn't as widely appealing once its release window passes, or when the deck's reprint value is poor.

A sort of mini-set within the greater Universes Beyond collection, the Assassin's Creed Universes Beyond contains 100 cards split across Beyond Boosters, a Starter Kit, a Bundle, and Collector Boosters, as well as two Secret Lairs. Beyond Boosters are a new type of Booster pack, and are not draftable but contain a mix of older cards with new artwork and original new cards designed with the Assassin's Creed games in mind.

The main thing working against Assassin's Creed is that it was released in the Eternal-only window for Universes Beyond, and this limited its potential to an almost redundant state. If given the proper Universes Beyond treatment in 2026, an Assassin's Creed set would be infinitely better and more relevant, but instead, this release is often forgotten.

The TMNT Universes Beyond set's one major redeeming quality is its draftability. It's a fun set to draft, but beyond that, it has a minimal impact on Standard and Commander.

Artistically, the set was perfect for the property it represented, and it even had some very cool chase cards in the form of the Kevin Eastman Borderless Signature turtles, but as a Magic set, especially one legal in the Standard format, TMNT is a letdown.

What has worked well and truly against TMNT is that it is sandwiched between two highly anticipated sets, Lorwyn Eclipsed and Secrets of Strixhaven, and both ended up being absolute blockbusters, making TMNT look meek in comparison.

This is easily one of the most divisive releases in Magic: The Gathering history, but at its core, it's shaping up to be a strong release in a few key ways. It's a highly draftable set, even if some of the ten combos are quite a bit stronger than others; it's still a fun set to build Limited decks with. Its Commander precon decks are also fairly impressive, with even the weakest of the decks being easily upgradable.

There are still four more Marvel-themed sets expected to be released in order to complete the full set of Infinity Stones.

The impact of this set on Standard and Commander in general will form over the coming months, and the result of this may change the ranking considerably, but for now, the Marvel Super Heroes set is trending far more positively than we expected, and it's going to make Wizards of the Coast a truckload of money.

The extremely popular Fallout series joined Magic: The Gathering with four Commander decks. The four decks follow a different faction or characters from the games, including Caesar and his Legion, the various mutants that populate the wastes, and even your favorite companion, Dogmeat.

In 2026, these decks are highly sought after and, for the most part, quite valuable. Fallout is a very popular property, so this was expected, but the limited nature of these Commander decks has led to some artificial pricing, especially given the overall power of some of the decks; it's all a bit disproportionate.

Regardless, the decks are well-built and themed, so if you can get your hands on one, they're a lot of fun to play with.

Love it, hate it, or simply don't care about it, the Avatar MTG set surpassed all expectations upon release in 2025 and was easily one of the most impactful Universes Beyond sets ever released, with the 2025 World Championship-winning deck largely featuring cards from the set in the Izzet Lessons archetype. Two of its biggest cards, Gran-Gran and Badgermole Cub, just got banned in Standard, too.

For Avatar fans, this set was a dream come true; for those with no attachment to the IP, it was a completely inoffensive crossover that produced unique card designs that became highly desirable in the print version of the game.

The Commander offering left a little to be desired, with no pre-con decks released, and a Commander's bundle available instead.

Given its smaller size, The Hobbit isn't going to leave the same lasting impression as the Tales of Middle-earth set, but that doesn't mean it isn't packed with exciting cards, a decent draft experience, and some big Commander additions and reprints. It feels like a continuation of the previous Lord of the Rings set, only this time it's Standard-legal.

The lack of any Commander precons was disappointing, as was the general size of the set, but given that this was turned around less than three years following the release of Tales of Middle-earth, it's actually quite an impressive feat.

Time will tell whether this set has any major impact on the Standard format, but we don't foresee any groundbreaking archetypes rising from the set. However, be sure to keep an eye on Goblins and Dwarves, both of which just got much more playable in Standard with the release of this set.

Any Middle-earth sets are going to rank highly just because they feel like a true Magic-adjacent property, and the cards always look and play great for the most part.

The Final Fantasy Universes Beyond crossover ended up being a huge hit with FF and MTG fans alike, largely because it was so clear to everyone that a lot of thought and planning had gone into the releases, and in reality, it was a hugely relevant deck in Standard at the time of release, with some powerful Mono-Green landfall and Gruul landfall decks still floating around using a few standout cards from the set.

On the Commander front, the FF VI Revival Trance deck is a major standout as one of the best Commander pre-con decks ever released, both out of the box and with minor upgrades.

There's a reason why this is the best-selling Magic set of all time, and while many purists may cringe at this fact, Final Fantasy will influence why Magic is the way it is for years to come.

#4082. Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business Review - Delivering Where It Matters

Australia Did It: End-of-the-world Railway Defense Business is a game I catch myself playing in my head long after I shut it off. Though it uses turn-based strategy as its base, it expands beyond the genre’s regular confines, blending elements from roguelikes, puzzle games, bullet-heaven titles, and the tower-defense genre. The result is an experience that demands wide-scale experimentation and rewards improvisation.

In a post-apocalyptic world where the Atlantic Ocean has dried up, you risk your life to ensure your shipment reaches its destination. Riding from station to station by train, you must build your team amid your many missions as various mutated creatures, malicious machines, and coordinated soldiers attack your convoy. Lore is doled out piecemeal and serves mostly as background dressing, but each time I learned more about the world, I became more curious.

To survive the harshness of the wasteland, you must use cindermint, an in-game resource gained for surviving turns and killing enemies, to spawn defenders, with three base classes to choose from. The revolver-wielding Gunslinger is your primary damage dealer, while the Radshot applies corrosive radiation damage, and the Nomad offers a close-range shotgun blast with knockback.

Those base-level characters offer solid variety upon which to build. And that’s where the main hook for Australia Did It comes in: experimentation through combination. In the midst of battle, you can merge two units of the same level to create new, more powerful defenders, influenced by the traits of those used in the merge. At the onset, you can merge two Nomads to create a level 2 Nomad with increased damage and knockback, but the real fun comes in combining disparate units to create completely new characters. Even now, more than 15 hours into my gameplay, I’m still concocting new combinations I want to try on my next run.

By the end of my first successful run, I had multiple level 6 characters, including a railgun-toting heavy, mages who steal health from enemies and redistribute it to nearby allies, a drone that can move beyond the walls of the station to attack enemies directly, and, my personal favorite, a dual-shotgun-wielding one-man wrecking crew. However, many of these higher-level units also possess drawbacks to consider, like the railgun scorching all adjacent tiles or the drone running out of battery if it’s outside the walls for too long. Though I started keeping notes in my head about which combinations led to my favorite results, I was grateful for a comprehensive compendium that tracked the tens of unit types I unlocked through this rewarding experimentation.

The meat of the experience places your squad on a 25-tile square board with enemies spawning from the four principal directions. Thoughtfulness and positioning are crucial, as each unit on your squad possesses different traits and movement efficiency, as do the encroaching enemies. Basic enemies often make a beeline toward the station, while others may take a weaving route or keep their distance and blast you at range. Improvising and adjusting your strategy on the fly is the most engaging part of Australia Did It, and when you perfectly adapt in the moment, or escape the scenario by the skin of your teeth, there are few better feelings I’ve experienced in a game this year.

Your goal in this phase is to simply defend the station and gather resources to strengthen your squad before evacuating and moving on to the next area. Considering each unit's strengths, weaknesses, and capabilities while strategically positioning them around the station takes some getting used to, especially during the more chaotic stages. I fist-pumped as I watched the train pull out of a station that was about to crumble, and I lamented the loss of high-level units I had to leave behind to ensure the survival of the convoy. The process is ceaselessly thrilling, even as you begin to see how the gears work under the hood. I just wish I could say the same about the intervening train sections.

Once you escape the turn-based strategy portion, your surviving squad members hop aboard the train and chart their route. Using a basic map, you choose your next stop, with factors like enemy types and modifiers shown to you ahead of time. The top-down train segments between station-defense stages are largely passive; the units you evacuated from the previous station automatically attack swarming enemies with the same traits and perks they have in the main gameplay areas. You can aim a focus cone to instruct your units, but you’re at the mercy of the units you’ve brought. You can trigger an ultimate ability to send your defenders into overdrive, but I rarely needed it.

While I love the idea of intentionally crafting a team that’s good at both the turn-based strategy and bullet-heaven transport sections, I was never fully engaged getting from point A to point B. Instead, I often caught myself checking how much longer before my train arrived at the next station; these sections can be completed in a minute or two, but that doesn’t alleviate the feeling that it’s a step down from the other gameplay. These novel portions aren’t bad by any means; they’re merely an average part of an otherwise excellent experience.

Looking back on the hours I poured into Australia Did It, the forgettable train segments will occupy only a small part of my memories, just as they do in each run. Instead, what will stick with me for months to come are the creative combination mechanics, the outstanding turn-based defense system, and the thrill of uncovering the mysteries of this bleak, yet engaging world.

#4081. Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

Battlefield 6's second-ever free trial, and the first in 2026, is upon us.

Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the new Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big new update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

#4079. Splatoon 3 Version 12.0.0 Update Out Now, Here Are The Full Patch Notes

The dev team also has another update on the way

Update [Wed 18th Nov 2026, 12:05am]: This new update for Splatoon 3 (Version 12.0.0) is now officially available to download. You can see the patch notes below.

Original Story: Nintendo's team-based squid-shooter Splatoon 3 is still going strong, and this week the title is getting updated to Version 12.0.0.

This major update will come with changes to multiplayer, including weapon adjustments. There are also changes to Anarchy Battle, X Battles and challenges. Additionally, there are changes to the GameChat feature on Switch 2. Nintendo also notes how its next update after this one will focus on multiplayer game balance.

You can get the full rundown in the official patch notes below (via Nintendo's official support page):

On this page: Splatoon 3 - Version 12.0.0 (17th November 2026)

Sections marked "on Nintendo Switch 2" apply only to Nintendo Switch 2. All other changes apply to both Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch.

Made it possible to participate with a friend in traditional X Battles as a group of two.

Added a feature that allows players to open GameChat and invite friends from their group while playing modes with friends, such as battles or Salmon Run.

This update focuses on making changes to matchmaking and multiplayer balance.

For X Battles, we have added a feature to allow players to play as a pair with a friend. The goal of this feature is to expand the range of ways to play, and we will introduce it on a trial basis starting in Chill Season 2026. After we have introduced it, we will comprehensively analyze how these battles are actually played and how the gameplay situation shifts, including for players who are not playing with a friend. Then we will decide whether to continue providing this feature in future seasons.

For Anarchy Battle (Series), we have changed the matchmaking system such that, in exchange for removing the feature allowing players to continue with the same team, matchmaking will now complete more quickly and with less imbalance of skill level and equipped weapons between players and their opponents.

For Challenges, we have changed how Challenge Power is calculated to make it easier to raise Challenge Power the more wins a player has. With this change, between players who would have ended up with about the same Challenge Power under the previous system, the player who attained the greater number of wins will have the higher final Challenge Power.

For multiplayer balance, we made a variety of changes to main, sub, and special weapons, including changes to the flight distance of Blaster shots.

With most weapons, when a player fires while moving, the player's movement speed is added to the shot's speed to a certain extent, resulting in a more natural trajectory. For Blasters, we have minimized the change in shot flight distance caused by this effect, making it easier to maintain an appropriate distance against an opponent’s Blaster.

Among the special weapons, we have changed the Reefslider because, while there is statistically little impact on victories in matches between extremely skilled players, it has a high impact on matches between less skilled players. The intention behind this change is to alleviate that striking difference. By narrowing the area affected by the explosion we have made it so that players cannot reap the maximum benefit without using it at the precise position. On the other hand, we have extended the invulnerability period to make it harder for opponents who used terrain to survive the explosion to counterattack and easier for the player to make follow-up attacks.

For the Tenta Missiles, we have decreased the vulnerability while firing and expanded the area where it is possible to lock on to opponents. As a result, it will now be easier to use, even in situations where opponents are nearby the player. By decreasing the impact interval, it becomes easier to defeat opponents who are slow to dodge, but the duration for which they must keep dodging is reduced.

We have also added a feature for Nintendo Switch 2 that will make it easier to use GameChat.

The next update will focus on changes to multiplayer balance.

If you haven't already played the game on Switch 2, there's a free upgrade available which includes visual improvements and frame rate optimisations for the platform. In some related news, Splatoon Raiders has also received an eShop demo this week!

#4078. Bandai Namco Shuts Down Unknown 9: Awakening Developer Reflector Entertainment

Bandai Namco has announced it is shutting down Reflector Entertainment, the Montreal studio behind 2024’s Unknown 9: Awakening.

Reflector, founded in 2015, is a subsidiary of Bandai Namco that was acquired in 2020. Unknown 9: Awakening is the studio’s only released title, which was first revealed at Gamescom 2020 and released on October 17, 2024. The third-person action game is set within the broader Unknown 9 transmedia franchise, which includes a book trilogy, comics, and a web series, and stars Haroona, a woman able to traverse a separate dimension called the Fold. Haroona, played by The Witcher actress Anya Chalotra, uses this ability and other supernatural powers to battle a hostile secret society across India and other global locations.

Upon release, Unknown 9: Awakening didn’t make much of a critical splash; it currently has a 59 Metascore and "Mixed" Steam reviews. In November 2024, a month after Unknown 9's launch, Reflector laid off 18 percent of its staff.  More layoffs were announced in January 2025 as Reflector canned an unannounced project while confirming Unknown 9 failed to meet expectations. With Reflector’s dissolution, Bandai Namco expects to post “an extraordinary loss” of approximately €21 million on its Q3 financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

#4077. PlayStation Cancels In-Development Live-Service Shooter, Fairgames, At Jade Raymond's Former Haven Studio

PlayStation has reportedly canceled Fairgames, the long-in-development live-service shooter being made by Haven Studios, which Jade Raymond founded in 2021. Sony acquired Haven in 2022, and in 2025, Raymond left the studio, though it remained dedicated to developing Fairgames without her. It seems the story of Fairgames is now over, according to a new Bloomberg report.

The publication reports that PlayStation will not enforce any job cuts or layoffs as a result of Fairgames' cancellation, which comes as a surprise, and the studio will instead shift to support other first-party teams under the PlayStation umbrella. According to Bloomberg, this cancellation comes after a recent test of the game that allowed "thousands of players" to check it out did not deliver the results PlayStation wanted.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email to employees today, according to Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

This doesn't necessarily come as a surprise. PlayStation announced Fairgames back in 2023 and hasn't shown much since, leaving many to assume development has been struggling behind the scenes. Since then, PlayStation has pulled back heavily on its live-service plans, which originally included launching more than 10 live-service games by March of this year. Naughty Dog's Last of Us multiplayer game was canceled, Bungie ended active development on Destiny 2, and live-service Horizon spin-off Hunters Gathering is reportedly being overhauled following poor playtest feedback, amongst other stories. Reading between the lines, many fans were waiting for news like today's cancellation of Fairgames to drop.

Still, in an era where games are canceled and entire teams are laid off (sometimes even after releasing a successful game), it's nice to see Haven employees are not facing layoffs.

#4076. MTG Star Trek Card Featuring Patrick Stewart Sells At $26K

Magic: The Gathering isn't exactly a stranger when it comes to ridiculously expensive cards, and while resellers aren't quite as rabid as some other TCGs, even somewhat less popular sets like Star Trek are still reaching hefty prices on the second-hand market. While the price might not compete with Lord of the Rings' over $2M One Ring card, getting one of MTG's new serialized cards will still cost you quite a bit.

While the seven hand-signed card variants introduced in MTG's Star Trek Collector's Boosters were already going to be a massive hit due to their limited availability, one of them has already broken the $20,000 mark, albeit for a bit of a morbid reason.

As shared by moombahh on Reddit, while most autographed Star Trek cards go for around $5-10K USD, a recent eBay listing for none other than Captain Jean-Luc Picard reportedly sold for a whopping $26K. While it's entirely possible the buyer sent a lower offer, it might even end up on the cheaper side of the spectrum if the other eBay listings are anything to go by.

With more recent listings having shot up all the way to $38K and an even more massive $45K, the price could wind up being well above the last sold price, and it's not hard to see why either.

For the first time ever, you can pack signed MTG cards, with seven to collect in total, but the first two revealed are of Captains Kirk and Janeway.

Dwarfing the Secret Lair card prices, the main reason players have been pricing their cards so high is that, since signing the cards, Jean-Luc Picard's actor, Patrick Stewart, recently passed away, leaving the serialized cards among the last items signed by the legendary actor.

While fans have pointed out that it's more than a little depressing that others are trying to capitalize on the late actor's passing by selling the cards for absurd prices, it's unlikely that sellers will be slowing down anytime soon, considering how limited their availability will continue to be.

#4075. The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Is Nintendo's Fastest-Selling Switch 2 Game Ever

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo's second remake of the original N64 game that first launched way back in 1998, is the fastest-selling Nintendo-published game on the Switch 2 ever. That accolade comes after the game sold more than 5.2 million copies in just four days following its November 5 launch last week.

This remake is already the Switch 2's second-best-selling Nintendo game at 5.2 million units sold, behind Mario Kart World's impressive 16.48 million copies sold to date. If The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time keeps this pace up, it could one day overtake Mario Kart World, though the Mario Kart series typically holds onto that top spot. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is still far and away the best-selling game on Switch.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the crown jewel of Nintendo's 40th Zelda series anniversary celebration, which also includes other games, products, and even an upcoming worldwide orchestral tour. Plus, a live-action Legend of Zelda film will debut in theaters worldwide on April 30, 2027.

Game Informer gave The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time a 9.25 out of 10 in its review, with our reviewer Kyle Hilliard writing, "For many like me, the original Ocarina of Time is an impactful adventure that arrived at a time in their lives when magic still felt real. Playing the game 28 years later and appreciating the care taken to maintain and improve the original vision was the ultimate surprise of the whole experience: I didn't expect to be so moved."

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched last week exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2.

For more, read this interview with the remake's producers about changes to the original game, easter eggs, the Bombchu bowling alley operator, and more, then check out this feature breaking down the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time easter eggs that did and didn't make it into this 2026 remake. After that, read about how the Switch 2 Pro controller can make The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time even better, then check out this interview with award-winning composer and musician Jon Batiste about the Ocarina of Time score.

Did you pick up The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time last week? Let us know what you think of it so far in the comments below!

#4074. Xbox CEO Pens New Message, Urges Platform Not To Get 'Trapped' By Its Proud History

Yesterday, we talked about the Project Helix part of the Xbox 25th anniversary magazine that's been made available to read in full on the official Xbox Wire website, and there's plenty more interesting stuff where that came from!

For example, the magazine kicks off with a statement from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who discusses the past 25 years of the brand and where it's going in the future - similar to a statement she shared on social media recently.

This time though, she talks less about how games will be made, and more about the fact that she wants to take "creative risks" while also acknowledging that her team won't "get every decision right" along the way.

"There are plenty of milestones from the past 25 years, and you'll find many of them in these pages. But I don't think the story of Xbox is really a story about any given hardware, launch or number. It is a story about people. Players turned games into friendships, rivalries and family traditions. They played with roommates who became lifelong friends, with brothers and sisters who moved across the country, with parents who got older and kids who eventually picked up the controller themselves. Some of the people we played with 25 years ago are no longer here. Some are sitting next to us, now playing with a new generation."

"We should be proud of that history. But we shouldn't be trapped by it."

"Games are alive. The best ones find new players and new creators. They move between generations. They get changed, remade and occasionally broken apart and rebuilt into something nobody expected. Twenty-five years in, Xbox should have that same restlessness."

"We have been given the chance to care for some of the most loved games and characters in the world. Our job is to protect what makes them special without protecting them from change. To keep making new things. To take creative risks. To meet players wherever they choose to play. And to make sure someone discovering Xbox for the first time today can feel the same possibility that someone felt turning on that first console in 2001."

"We don't get every decision right. No company that is still making things does. But we can keep listening, learning and building. Twenty-five years ago, a relatively small group of people imagined that Microsoft could make a game console. It was an improbable idea. They made it real. I like that as our inheritance."

There's definitely some interesting stuff in here, including Sharma's insistence that Xbox shouldn't be "trapped" by its past, that her team should be willing to experiment and take risks in the future, and an admission that not every decision will work out for the best. That's pretty refreshing to hear, and it certainly reads well on paper at least.

Let's see what happens, eh? Xbox's 25th anniversary has been a weird year, full of ups and downs, but it seems like there's a cautious optimism circulating around the fanbase regarding things like console updates, exclusives and various other initiatives that have been introduced since the Xbox CEO took the helm at the start of the year.

These next 25 years are going to be fascinating to say the least!

#4073. Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds Free McLaren Racing Update Adds New Sonic Skin And Machine

Sega's all-star racing game Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds has this week received a new McLaren Racing-themed update.

It includes Sonic in a McLaren Racing suit and the speed-type McLaren Racing machine. There's also a McLaren Racing festival taking place. Here's the rundown:

"Players can now race around the track for pole position as Sonic in the iconic papaya and anthracite McLaren livery. Starting Thursday, November 19 at 4:00 PM PT and until Sunday, November 29 at 3:59 PM PT, fans can jump into the McLaren Racing festival and earn festival points for decals, gadgets and more!"

Along with this, Sega has announced a new "3-episode animated special" is on the way. You can see the teaser trailer for Sonic the Hedgehog x McLaren Racing: Beyond Fast" in the video above.

This is the second update of the 'Year Two' content. It follows the release of Bayonetta alongside the launch of this new season. Aigis will follow in "early 2027". Here's what else is planned in terms of free and paid content:

#4072. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.1 livestream reveals a pared-back, four-week update as HoYo plays catch-up

Honkai: Star Rail will continue the Planarcadia story arc in Version 4.1, as the Star Rail Fest presents a new twist.

A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a new activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Finally, Version 4.1 marks the start of a new Arcadian Chronicles phase in the Divergent Universe. You’ll be able to use Waypoint Pass cards to explore the different areas. HoYo is also bringing back Planar Fissure and Garden of Plenty with double rewards. And as ever, if you log in for at least seven days after downloading the new patch, you’ll earn 10 premium banner pulls.

#4071. Marvel 1943: Rise Of Hydra Reportedly Still In Development Amid Rumors Of Its Cancellation

Yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, new reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was quickly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance New Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

However, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance New Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

Kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

This isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-new globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no announced platforms.

Although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

#4070. Where To Play Every Game Of The Year Nominee For 2026

The votes have been cast and the nominees for 2026's Game of the Year have been revealed. Six of the past year's biggest and best games, and as always, the games that have and haven't made the cut are being hotly debated. There's also a remake in the mix this year along with a game that hadn't been released when the nominations were announced, so a lot for those who think the awards should have clearer criteria to discuss.

Whether you agree with all six nominees or not, it's hard to argue that the games in the running this year aren't six of the six biggest games released this calendar year. The games that, if you haven't played anything else this year, or if there are some you missed, you should probably try your best to play before we get to 2027 and another year of new games begins. Whether you're wondering whether you have the right hardware before buying the nominees, want to know if they have a physical release, or you just want to know how much they cost, you'll find everything you need to know to fill in your GOTY gaps below.

GTA 6 is finally here, and its Game of the Year nomination has caused a stir. The game will be here by the time the awards are handed out, but it was nominated two days before release. That doesn't matter to you right now, though. The launch of GTA 6 is mere hours away as I type this, and if you're not one of the 15 million people who have placed a pre-order, here's what you need to know.

As long as you ignore the state of rent, wages, and world economics, GTA 6's price tag isn't that bad, you guys!

GTA 6 will only be available on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S when released. Its PC launch will follow at a later, still unrevealed, time. There are two editions to choose from - standard and ultimate. The standard edition will provide tens, if not hundreds, of hours of entertainment, but there will be various stores, barbers, and tattoo parlors that are off-limits if you don't own the ultimate edition.

The standard edition of GTA 6 is $79.99 on both PS5 and Series X|S, while the ultimate edition is $99.99 on both platforms.

GTA 6 isn't the only game that has caused a stir by picking up a GOTY nomination this year. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has poked the beehive that is remakes being eligible to win the prestigious award. If there was ever a remake that was going to qualify, it's a universally loved one like this that somehow reimagines one of the greatest games of all time without upsetting any of the original's fans.

There is only one place you can play the Ocarina of Time remake, and that's on Switch 2. There are no different editions to choose from, but there is a physical release, and since this is a Switch 2 exclusive, there's a price difference between its digital and physical versions. A digital copy of Ocarina of Time costs $59.99, but if you want a physical copy, it'll cost you $69.99.

Robert Pattinson might be the next James Bond on the big screen, but Patrick Gibson became the video game Bond this year in the critically acclaimed 007 First Light. A performance so good that not only were fans suggesting Gibson could potentially make the jump to Bond movies, but the odds of that happening spiked significantly after the game was released.

First Light is the first nominee on the list that's available to play on Steam. It's also on PS5 and Series X|S, and while a Switch 2 version was promised, it has been delayed until March 18, 2027. I have played a little bit of the game on Switch 2, and for what it's worth, I didn't encounter any issues and was a little surprised that its release was moved into 2027.

It's amazing to see just how far this series has come since the low point that was Resident Evil 6. The trilogy that has followed, alongside the remakes of games from its heyday, has put Resident Evil firmly back on top of the video game mountain. That's why Resident Evil Requiem, a game many would describe as the best new Resi game in decades, is in the running to be crowned Game of the Year.

If you're trying to play all of these games before a winner is crowned, or you want to get one under your belt quickly, Requiem is the place to start. By far the shortest nominee on this year's GOTY list, with a story that takes around 11 hours to play through according to How Long To Beat. It's also the only one of all six nominees that's available on all major platforms, with those who played on Switch 2 awarding it, and Capcom's other day-one Switch 2 releases this year, high praise.

Phantom Blade Zero is a game people have been waiting a long time for. Shown off for the first time well over three years ago, S-Game's action-packed epic finally arrived in October, and it did not disappoint. Rave reviews and a player base that wholeheartedly agrees with what the critics had to say about it have landed it among 2026's Game of the Year nominees.

Your platform options are limited for this one - just PS5 for console players, but it is on PC too if you prefer to play there. There's no physical release either, which is unfortunate, although a physical edition of the PS5 version has been promised for 2027. Hopefully there aren't any issues getting that out on time, with PlayStation pushing forward with its promise to stop putting games on discs in 2028.

Control Resonant might be the most surprising inclusion among this year's Game of the Year nominees. Not because it doesn't deserve to be on this list, but because it's the only game of the six where the combined reaction to its release wasn't overwhelmingly positive, unlike the other five. Not that many people had anything negative to say about it, just that it didn't seem to blow everyone away quite as much as its GOTY competitors.

Now that said, if you want to play the best games 2026 has to offer, Control Resonant should unquestionably be on your list, particularly if you liked the first game and you're an Alan Wake fan. It's available on PS5, Xbox, and PC, there's a physical version if you're into that kind of thing, and it's slightly more expensive and includes an extra outfit, resources, and a digital artbook and soundtrack.

Steam has incredible sales all year round, but nothing quite compares to the deals you can get during the holiday season!

#4069. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.7 brings Angels of Delusion to the battlefield with playable Nangong Yu

Champions Never Fall to the Past indeed, as Zenless Zone Zero prepares for a major update that fans of Angels of Delusion will appreciate.

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier quickly.

Our first new arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

#4068. Halo: Campaign Evolved Gets Firefight Mode In Free Update This Winter

Halo: Campaign Evolved is getting the fan-favorite Firefight mode via a free update this winter, an Xbox Wire post announces. The update will allow players to team up in cooperative wave-based PvE.

Firefight, which debuted in Halo 3: ODST, lets up to four players team up to survive waves of enemies. The mode has become a popular staple and has appeared in multiple Halo games, but this will be the first time that it has been retroactively added to the original entry.

Xbox FanFest attendees, a global multi-city event, will be the first to go hands-on with Campaign Evolved’s take on Firefight. Additionally, more details about Firefight will be shared during Halo Fest in Seattle on December 12-13, where the mode will also be playable for attendees.

#4067. 'We've Heard You!' - Star Wars Galactic Racer Is Officially Adding Split-Screen Multiplayer

An incredible addition to an incredible game

Star Wars Galactic Racer is my favourite game of the year so far. It's an incredible racing title that even surpasses the original Star Wars Episode 1 Racer in my view, and I've had so much fun with the campaign and online multiplayer.

There's just one downside that everyone's been pointing out since it was revealed, and that's the absence of local split-screen multiplayer. With that in mind, the development team have found a way to implement it in a new update.

The update isn't available yet, but will be coming to the game in early 2027. Alongside it will be a new mode called Free Play, which is where you'll be able to freely choose your vehicle, character, planet and race track.

"We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to STAR WARS: Galactic Racer. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action."

It seems Free Play is the only place where you'll be able to access local split-screen multiplayer in Star Wars Galactic Racer, but that's no surprise considering how solo-focused the main campaign is. They'd literally have to rewrite massive portions of the campaign if they were going to implement split-screen into it.

Anyway, this is just an amazing bonus on top of an already amazing game, and I encourage you to check it out if you enjoy a title like Burnout 3: Takedown - it's fast-paced and frantic, has the same kind of takedown system that you'll remember from that game, and the roguelite campaign is really well designed (online is great fun as well).

If you've played it, let us know what you think of the game in the poll down below!

#4066. Pokémon Champions Is Getting A Balance Patch Next Month

The Pokémon Company has announced the free-to-play Switch and mobile game Pokémon Champions is getting a balance update next month on 2nd December 2026.

This balance update will include move updates and adjustments. Here's the rundown about the moves certain Pokémon will now have access to. Along with this are details about the adjustments to select moves (via Nintendo Everything).

The following Pokémon will be able to use the moves listed here

Psych Up: Alakazam, Starmie, Mr. Mime, Mawile, Altaria, Castform, Absol, Roserade, Weavile, Rotom, Rotom (Heat Rotom), Rotom (Wash Rotom), Rotom (Frost Rotom), Rotom (Fan Rotom), Rotom (Mow Rotom), Liepard, Musharna, Audino, Cofagrigus, Slurpuff, Drampa, Annihilape

Play Rough: Vaporeon, Jolteon, Flareon, Espeon, Umbreon, Leafeon, Glaceon

#4065. Wolfenstein 3 Is Officially In Production

Wolfenstein 3 is officially underway at MachineGames, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced.

The announcement of the third mainline Wolfenstein title in MachineGames’ trilogy comes over seven years after the launch of the fourth and most recent spin-off entry, Wolfenstein: Youngblood. Sharma’s announcement includes a teaser image of the script for Wolfenstein 3's first chapter. MachineGames echoed this reveal with its own post, which includes a photo of a motion capture session featuring actress Debra Wilson, who plays Grace Walker in the series.

Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames. One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more. https://t.co/YyX8LrbTvh

MachineGames’ last release was 2024’s well-received Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, but studio co-founder Jerk Gustafsson stated in a NoClip documentary last year that he hoped to finish BJ Blazkowicz’s story. Based on Gustafsson’s comment, it sounds like Wolfenstein 3 very recently started production, so we probably shouldn’t expect any substantial update for a good while.

This won’t be the only new Wolfenstein project, as Amazon is developing a live-action series based on the franchise. Until either the new game or the show releases, you can tide yourself over by reading our reviews of Wolfenstein: The New Order, Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus, and Wolfenstein: Youngblood.

#4064. Heartopia goes to the movies with its next event

Heartopia's Whale Island will soon host a new event that's all about the magic of cinema.

Heartopia’s next in-game event has been announced, and it’s one you may not have seen coming. Developer XD Games revealed Dreamlight Cinematics Festival, an upcoming limited-time event that celebrates cinema and movie-making.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

If you log in during the event’s runtime, you’ll get the Car Cinema furniture set for free. This cosmetic bundle comes with chairs that are modelled after vintage vehicles, as well as poster display stands with unique movie making-themed decorations.

If you’re looking to spend some money, the Deluxe Festival Pack comes with a large Island Sunset Billboard, which you can place outside your home so everyone knows you spent that money. The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

For now, we have the above reveal trailer to go on, which does offer some idea of what it’s going to look like in-game. Until things kick off on the weekend, you best arm yourself with some Heartopia codes.

#4063. Lego And TT Games Seemingly Tease A New Lego James Bond Game

The Lego games have been a part of many gamers' childhoods, but TT Games has more than proven in recent years that their family-friendly gaming adaptations can be enjoyed by just about anyone regardless of their age. While rumors have been circulating about what the next Lego gaming project would be after it was leaked to be a Warner Bros. property, some recent teases have fans thinking otherwise.

While it's far from an official confirmation of any kind, both TT Games and Lego themselves chiming in on the topic already has fans fully convinced that a previously cancelled Lego game could be getting the modern-day return it desperately deserves.

First spotted by CrazyLegoMoment on X, a suspicious series of tweets was made after it was announced Robert Pattinson would be taking the mantle of James Bond moving forward, starting with TT Games responding with a pair of eyes emoji when Shai Matheson (voice of Batman in Lego Batman: Legacy of The Dark Knight) joked that he would be "the next Lego Bond".

As if that wasn't enough, even the official Lego account responded by saying "he's got a license to build" when another fan posted about wanting an official Lego James Bond game made by TT Games.

Legacy of the Dark Knight has clocked up impressive enough review scores to make it the highest-rated Lego game ever.

While these could certainly just be some members of the studios trying to join in on the viral sensation and memes coming out of the news, an official announcement wouldn't be much of a surprise considering TT Games had already pitched several James Bond-themed Lego games in the past, one of which saw its entire pitch trailer leaked last year to the excitement of countless fans.

Having supposedly rejected TT Games' take on Bond for the subject material being "too mature" for the Lego in the past, the company has since branched out to countless adult franchises for official sets and even triple-A games like Legacy of The Dark Knight that Bond would feel right at home with for a full-blown adaptation.

Combined with the unique gameplay mechanics, open-world, and sheer level of detail offered by TT Games' previous Legacy of the Dark Knight and Skywalker Saga, a standalone Lego James Bond game would be a perfect fit with countless vehicles, gadgets, and costumes to experiment with.

With 27 films over the past 60 years to pull from, a Lego James Bond game isn't exactly starved for potential when it comes to levels and characters either, which would also offer the perfect tie-in game for whenever Robert Pattinson's upcoming Bond film releases.

#4062. All the hype has already made Crimson Desert one of the biggest launches on Steam this year

We're merely days away from the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Crimson Desert has come in clutch to join the list of big sellers.

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”

#4060. God Of War Sons Of Sparta Gets PS4 Version And New Content Next Monday

It's been about nine months since Sony Santa Monica and Mega Cat Studios dropped God of War Sons of Sparta as a surprise reveal and launch during a State of Play. If you haven't checked it out yet, the developers are giving you some new reasons to today, unveiling two new modes and a new platform: PlayStation 4.

If you don't remember, God of War Sons of Sparta is a prequel spin-off of the God of War series, showing protagonist Kratos as a 13-year-old soldier, long before his god-killing days. The game features 2D combat and a Metroidvania-style map, along with a fully voiced cast of characters including Scott Menville (who you might recognize as Robin in Teen Titans) as Kratos' brother Deimos, Jack Quaid (who will voice a different character in God of War Laufey next year), and TC Carson, who returns from the original trilogy as the voice of adult Kratos.

Announced in a post on the PlayStation Blog today, Sons of Sparta is making the jump back to Sony's previous console, which is now (brace yourself) 13 years old. Sons of Sparta's 2D pixel art is far less demanding than the other God of War entries, though, so it's no surprise this was possible – it's mainly surprising that they're doing it at all.

For PS5 players who already own the game, developer Mega Cat is also adding two new modes: Hermes Mode and Erebus Mode. Hermes Mode, named after the Greek god of wind, mail, and speed, is a speedrun mode that encourages you to beat the game as quickly as possible, complete with a split-based timer in the upper right-hand corner of the screen. Meanwhile, Erebus Mode, named after one of the domains of the underworld (you'll be familiar with it if you've played the Hades games), makes the game far deadlier as Kratos and all his foes die in a single hit. You'll have to wait until you beat the game once to unlock Erebus Mode, but you can access Hermes Mode from a fresh save by entering the following (and semi-familiar) code in the start menu: Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, L1, R1, Touchpad.

The free update and PS4 version will be available next Monday, November 16, at midnight local time. For more Sons of Sparta, check out our review. For more God of War, bad news: God of War Laufey was just delayed until May.

#4059. Poll: What Do You Think The Metacritic Score Will Be For GTA 6?

Considering we're just a few days away from the release of GTA 6 on November 19th, we're bound to start getting reviews at some point between now and launch, and it'll be fascinating to see what the critics think of it!

This is a series that has consistently dominated on Metacritic over the years - a website that takes loads of professional reviews and creates an average score based around them. Grand Theft Auto V has a 97 average rating on there, for example, while GTA 4 goes even higher with a 98 rating.

In fact, every mainline release since GTA 3 (not including stuff like Chinatown Wars and Liberty City Stories) has reached at least a 95 on the platform. To put that into context, the best-rated Xbox Series X game of the year on Metacritic right now is Hades 2, and that game has a 95 average rating.

Feature These Are Xbox's Best 25 Games From 2001-2026 According To Metacritic

If we're going off history alone, GTA 6 has every chance of becoming the highest-reviewed game of 2026 on Xbox and PS5. The question is whether it'll manage to hit those highs once again, or whether it'll struggle to meet the hype.

Let's not forget there's never been a wait like this for a GTA game before, and while absence definitely does make the heart grow fonder, it also creates a sense of expectation that's extremely difficult to live up to.

We'll have to wait and see what happens! You'll find a review roundup on Pure Xbox ASAP, and it seems the smart bet is at least a 95 rating on Metacritic, although that's much easier said than achieved.

For reference, here are some other Metacritic scores from GTA games in the past:

Guide GTA 6 Release Times: All The Key Details Xbox Players Need To Know

#4058. Helldivers 2 Devs Say Bouncy Stratagem Fix Is Still “In Development”

Helldivers 2 has had a rollercoaster of fan reactions since its release, flipping between one of the most hyped PvE games in recent years and an incredibly controversial sci-fi shooter. While much of this criticism springs from just how popular and surprising the success story behind Helldivers 2 is compared to its predecessor, Arrowhead Studios still seems to be working on issues that have been plaguing the game since release.

This isn't to say that fans have been starving for content, with a whole new faction, numerous collaborations, and plenty of live-service events to keep them busy, but even dedicated members of the community are feeling frustrated by just how long it took for Helldivers 2's upcoming gameplay change.

If you've ever played Helldivers 2 before, you'll definitely have encountered the problem of throwing down a Stratagem on a rocky surface, or even a flat building, before it winds up bouncing dozens of meters away from where you intended.

While you might have assumed this was an intended feature to limit their effectiveness, Arrowhead Studios themselves have revealed it's actually a bug on X that they're actively working to fix.

Rather than being happy about the change, fans have been using it as a point of criticism over wondering how they are expected to be "hyped over a bug fix that should've happened in 2024," alongside other players noting that "modders fixed this and hellpod steering long ago."

As if that wasn't enough, the long-awaited bug fix is not even being added to the game yet, with "more information coming in the new year" to the disappointment of many players.

While it's still certainly great to see Helldivers still getting updates and quality of life fixes years after release, it's not hard to see why players are so frustrated either, especially after the implementation of stricter anti-cheat that ended up disabling countless fan-made mods.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4057. Crimson Desert's first patch aims at fixing controls, but it mostly affects mouse and keyboard

The first post-launch patch for Crimson Desert is here, and the list of changes is promising, even if it doesn't go far enough to address some deeper issues.

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”

Today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

This latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

The most important changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added new pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

#4056. Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns Of The Patriots: Part 8 – A Nostalgic Island Getaway | Super Replay

In 2008, Kojima Productions released what was billed as the swan song for Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear series: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots. The game had the staggering task of tying up decades of storytelling by bringing together Solid Snake, Ocelot, Otacon, Raiden, and many more characters for one explosive finale. The adventure centers on a rapidly aging Solid Snake racing against the clock to stop his twin and nemesis, Liquid Snake, one last time. Of course, there are far more bizarre shenanigans at play.

Guns of the Patriots was acclaimed for its storytelling, cinematic presentation, and evolution of the series' stealth gameplay, namely the OctoCamo suit that allowed Snake to mimic the appearance/texture of any surface he touched. It also has the distinct honor of earning a rare 10/10 review score from Game Informer. Now, thanks to the Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2, we can finally revisit MGS 4 without dusting off a PlayStation 3.

Join recent Metal Gear convert Charles Harte, who will be on the sticks to experience Guns of the Patriots (via the Master Collection Vol. 2) for the very first time, alongside long-time series fan Marcus Stewart, who is revisiting MGS 4 for the first time in over a decade. The stream kicks off today live on Twitch and YouTube at 12 p.m. PT/3 p.m. ET, and will continue for two hours each week until we roll credits.

If you can't catch us live, you can watch each episode after they air by following the YouTube links below.

Every week, Game Informer editors enter the vault and dust off games from every genre and platform imaginable. Watch Replay to relive fond (and not so fond) memories from gaming’s past.

#4054. Stalker 2’s first expansion officially revealed, and it's taking us to the power plant where it all began

Stalker 2’s first add-on isn’t far off, and it may just be the thing to bring you back to post-apocalyptic Chornobyl in 2026.

One of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the new Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the big news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

The story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

GSC Game World says Cost of Hope will introduce two new regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two new regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

The developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.
